<a id="s0-p1"></a>[0¶1] This document states what pcrec's library (`lib/pcrec.h`) and every
generated matcher promise. It is the contract: present tense, normative,
and the only authority on the match API. Design documents it points at
(`docs/design/…`) are informational background, never a second source of
authority; where one disagrees with this document, this document is what
pcrec promises. How the contract came to be — rulings, panels, earlier
wordings, the `abi` change log — is not here: it is in
`docs/dev/history/match_api_record.md` and
`docs/dev/history/abi_changelog.md`, neither of which is normative.

<a id="s0-p2"></a>[0¶2] **Citing this document.** The number is the citation. Every
section has one (its heading's, `§3.1.3`) and every paragraph has one within
its section, written `§3.1.3¶4` and shown as the `[3.1.3¶4]` label at the
paragraph's start. A paragraph is a prose paragraph, a list item or a block
quote, numbered from 1 in document order within its innermost section (`§0`
is this preamble); a code block or a table belongs to the paragraph it
follows, or to its section when nothing precedes it. Cite
`match_api.md §3.1.3¶4`, never a line number. Numbers are permanent: a section
added between §3.2 and §3.3 is `§3.2a`, a paragraph added after ¶4 is `¶4a`
(the first paragraph of `§3.2a` is `§3.2a¶1`), and a removal leaves the
one-line stub `§N — retired` under the same number, so a citation that was
true stays resolvable. Each number is also a link target: `#s3-1-3` for the
section, `#s3-1-3-p4` for the paragraph. The contents above are generated
from the headings by `scripts/spec_toc.py`; `docs/spec/CLAUDE.md` states the
numbering rule for every spec document.

<a id="s0-p3"></a>[0¶3] **What the statements rest on.** Every rule below is checked against the
shipped surface: `lib/pcrec.h`, artifacts emitted by `build/pcrec`, and the
suites named inline. Where a sentence says *measured*, the number is
evidence the contract rests on, reproduced by the cited suite or probe.

<a id="s0-p4"></a>[0¶4] **Pre-v1 posture (D40).** This contract carries no backwards-compatibility
weight yet. Breaking changes are unconstrained in substance and governed
only in form: one announced-boundary commit per break, populations conserved
and accounted, never silent drift. For an emitted-scaffolding change the
announced boundary is the `abi` bump itself (§6¶17). At a future
v1 declaration this document, or its direct successor, becomes the
compatibility-bound enumeration.

---

<a id="s1"></a>
## 1. Symbols and namespaces

<a id="s1-p1"></a>[1¶1] Every symbol a pattern compile can produce falls into one of three groups.

<a id="s1-p2"></a>[1¶2] **1. Per-artifact symbols**, scoped by the caller's `pcrec_options.prefix`
(default `"rx"`): the entry points `<prefix>_search`, `<prefix>_match`,
`<prefix>_match_caps`, `<prefix>_search_in`, `<prefix>_match_in`,
`<prefix>_match_caps_in`, `<prefix>_next_pos`, `<prefix>_valid_upto`, the
data symbol `<prefix>_info`, the `<prefix>_buffers` type, every other
emitted identifier (helpers, tables, the named-group array), and the
`<PREFIX>_*` macro family (`<PREFIX>_NCAPS`, the sizing macros of §10.4, the
stamp macros of §6.3). A pattern compiled with `-p foo` gets `foo_search`,
`FOO_NCAPS`, and so on. The CLI spells the option `-p` only; there is no
`--prefix` long form (`pcrec --prefix foo …` is an unknown-option error).
`docs/spec/cli.md` gives `-p`'s identifier grammar. Every other emitted
identifier — helper functions, tables, the DFA state types and their
accessors, labels — is prefix-scoped and INTERNAL: its name, shape and
linkage are not part of this contract and may change at any `abi` bump.

<a id="s1-p3"></a>[1¶3] **2. pcrec's own fixed library surface**: the `PCREC_*` enum and bit
constants and the `pcrec_options` / `pcrec_output` / `pcrec_error` /
`pcrec_err_input` types declared in `lib/pcrec.h`. These are never scoped by
a pattern's prefix.

<a id="s1-p4"></a>[1¶4] `PCREC_*` names only pcrec's own enum- or bit-valued constants — never a
struct field name, never a bare CLI flag spelling — with one exception: every
artifact carries `PCREC_FEATURE_SET` and `PCREC_FEATURE_MODULES` (the D37
artifact stamp, e.g. `#define PCREC_FEATURE_SET "std1"`, `#define
PCREC_FEATURE_MODULES "classes,modifiers"`), which are `PCREC_*`-named,
PER-ARTIFACT, and declared nowhere in `lib/pcrec.h`. An artifact is never
ambiguous about what it was built with. The exported default feature set is
the lower-case data symbol `pcrec_default_features` (§8.2). `PCRE2_*`
spellings are reserved for a future PCRE2-compatibility layer and are never
native.

<a id="s1-p5"></a>[1¶5] **3. The shared ABI block**: fixed-literal types and contract constants,
scoped by neither of the above. In declaration order the types are
`rx_var`, `rx_ctx`, `rx_matchfn`, `rx_callout_ref`, `rx_renderfn`,
`rx_group_entry` and `struct rx_info`. They are spelled `rx_*` regardless of
the prefix, so that two differently-prefixed matchers compose in one
translation unit (one matcher links directly as another's callout, with no
adapter). They live inside their own `PCREC_RX_ABI_H` guard, separate from
the per-prefix `PCREC_GEN_<PREFIX>_H` guard around the rest of the header,
and `-p rx` and `-p foo` builds of one pattern emit byte-identical blocks.

<a id="s1-p6"></a>[1¶6] The same block carries every emitted macro whose VALUE is a pcrec-contract
fact rather than a per-artifact one, unprefixed and emitted unconditionally
on every artifact, a DFA-only one included: the give-up and refusal codes
(`PCREC_ERR_*`, §4), the caps unset sentinel `PCREC_UNSET` (§5), the engine
constants `PCREC_ENGINE_DFA` / `PCREC_ENGINE_VM` (§6), and the nine stamp
bit constants `PCREC_VM_RUNG_*` / `PCREC_VM_STRAT_*` / `PCREC_VM_PRUNE_*`
(§6.3). No per-prefix spelling of any of them exists. What stays per-prefix
is exactly what varies per artifact: `<PREFIX>_NCAPS`, the stamp macros
(including the three masks), and the budget, capacity and sizing macros.

<a id="s1-p7"></a>[1¶7] **The guard's value is the `abi`, and a mixed-`abi` translation unit is
refused.** The block opens

```c
#if defined(PCREC_RX_ABI_H) && (PCREC_RX_ABI_H + 0) != 71
#error "pcrec: this artifact (abi 71) shares a translation unit with an artifact of a different abi; regenerate both with one pcrec"
#endif
#ifndef PCREC_RX_ABI_H
#define PCREC_RX_ABI_H 71
```

so artifacts of one `abi` share the first block, and an artifact of another
`abi` (whose types may differ) fails to compile, naming the cause. `+ 0`
makes the test refuse an artifact older than `abi` 54 included first (its
guard is defined empty); an artifact older than 54 included AFTER a newer
one is not refused, because its own `#ifndef` predates the rule.

<a id="s1-p8"></a>[1¶8] **Self-contained and split artifacts.** An artifact is either one
self-contained `.c` (`pcrec_options.header_name == NULL`; the CLI's `-o -`)
or a `.c` with a paired `.h` (`header_name` set; the CLI's `-o FILE.c`
writes `FILE.h` beside it). Both forms carry the same declarations. The
self-contained form has no `PCREC_GEN_<PREFIX>_H` guard (there is no header
to guard). In the split form the `.h` carries the shared ABI block,
`<PREFIX>_NCAPS`, the sizing macros of §10.4, the `<prefix>_buffers` type,
the entry declarations and, on a variable-bearing artifact,
`<PREFIX>_NVARS` and its index macros; the stamp macros of §6.3 are emitted
into the `.c` only ([stamp scoping](#s6-3-1)).

---

<a id="s2"></a>
## 2. Fixed ABI types

<a id="s2-p1"></a>[2¶1] The shared block, verbatim from a default `-p rx` artifact of `'a(b|c)+d'`
(only `struct rx_info`'s body is elided here; §6 lists it field by field):

```c
typedef struct rx_var {
    const char          *name;  /* NUL-terminated; the pattern's own
                                    spelling of the name */
    const unsigned char *p;     /* NULL == UNSET. When p is NULL, len
                                    is IGNORED and never read. */
    size_t               len;   /* bytes; 0 with p != NULL == EMPTY */
} rx_var;

typedef struct rx_ctx {
    const unsigned char *subject;   /* whole subject, not a slice */
    size_t                len;      /* subject length */
    size_t                pos;      /* where to match, anchored */
    size_t                ncap;     /* capture slots known so far (watermark
                                        mid-match; ncaps on completion) */
    const ptrdiff_t     (*caps)[2]; /* [start,end); {-1,-1} = unset */
    void                 *user;     /* per-binding user data */
    const rx_var         *vars;     /* caller variables, by NAME;
                                        NULL when none */
    size_t                nvars;    /* entries in vars[] */
} rx_ctx;

/* returns matched length >= 0 (anchored at ctx->pos), -1 (fail), or a
 * typed give-up code in [PCREC_ERR_FLOOR, -2] -- one per way the
 * engine can give up (PCREC_ERR_STEPS/_FRAMES/_WORK/_RECURSE). D49: those
 * codes PROPAGATE, they are not collapsed to -1, and a caller doing
 * an exact `== -1` test sees them as distinct values. Values
 * strictly BELOW PCREC_ERR_FLOOR stay RESERVED for a future abort
 * semantic; PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL ([DD-14] wave A commit 2, D71
 * item 1) is its first producer -- the artifact's own
 * inconsistency check firing, never a resource give-up -- and a
 * generated call site that invokes an rx_matchfn traps on one.
 * Self-contained: must accept ctx->ncap == 0, ctx->caps == NULL. */
typedef ptrdiff_t rx_matchfn(const rx_ctx *ctx);

#define PCREC_ERR_STEPS   (-2)
#define PCREC_ERR_FRAMES  (-3)
#define PCREC_ERR_WORK    (-4)
#define PCREC_ERR_RECURSE (-5)  /* [DD-14] reserved: no producer yet (D71 item 1) */
#define PCREC_ERR_FLOOR   (-5)  /* give-ups: [FLOOR,-2]; below: reserved (D49) */

#define PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL (-6)  /* [DD-14] below PCREC_ERR_FLOOR: NOT a give-up, D71 item 1 */
#define PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS (-7)  /* [K50] below PCREC_ERR_FLOOR: NOT a give-up -- a mid-character startpos was REFUSED */
#define PCREC_ERR_UNSET_VAR (-8)  /* [VAR] below PCREC_ERR_FLOOR: NOT a give-up -- an UNSET or ill-formed variable value was REFUSED */
#define PCREC_ERR_UTF (-9)  /* [UTF-VALID] below PCREC_ERR_FLOOR: NOT a give-up -- an ill-formed subject was REFUSED (-futf-check) */

#define PCREC_UNSET ((ptrdiff_t)-1)

typedef struct rx_callout_ref {
    rx_matchfn *fn;
    void       *user;
} rx_callout_ref;

/* Emitted ONLY when a substitution template names it. Renders one
 * template segment from the same rx_ctx a callout receives. Writes at
 * most outcap bytes to out; returns the number of bytes produced, or
 * -1 to fail. Called with out == NULL and outcap == 0, it returns the
 * length it WOULD produce, writing nothing. */
typedef ptrdiff_t rx_renderfn(const rx_ctx *ctx,
                              unsigned char *out, size_t outcap);

typedef struct {
    const char *name;
    int         number;
    int         slot;   /* caps[] index this entry delivers, or -1 if
                           this build delivers no slot for it */
    const char *ref;    /* NULL/empty for the primary's own groups */
} rx_group_entry;

struct rx_info {
    /* ... §6 ... */
};

#define PCREC_ENGINE_DFA 1
#define PCREC_ENGINE_VM  2

#define PCREC_VM_RUNG_CURSOR           0x1u
#define PCREC_VM_RUNG_FRAMES_BOUNDED   0x2u
#define PCREC_VM_RUNG_FRAMES_UNBOUNDED 0x4u
#define PCREC_VM_RUNG_REVDET           0x8u
#define PCREC_VM_RUNG_COUNTER          0x10u
#define PCREC_VM_STRAT_POSSESSIVE      0x1u
#define PCREC_VM_STRAT_BACKTRACKING    0x2u
#define PCREC_VM_PRUNE_CLAMPED         0x1u
#define PCREC_VM_PRUNE_UNCLAMPED       0x2u
```

<a id="s2-p2"></a>[2¶2] The block ends with a comment describing `<prefix>_next_pos` and then
`#endif /* PCREC_RX_ABI_H */`. `extern const struct rx_info <prefix>_info;`
is per-prefix and is declared outside the block.

<a id="s2-p3"></a>[2¶3] What the block's comments state, made explicit:

- <a id="s2-p4"></a>[2¶4] **`rx_matchfn`'s return space** is §4's: a matched length `>= 0`
  anchored at `ctx->pos`, `-1` for no match, a give-up code in
  `[PCREC_ERR_FLOOR, -2]`, or a below-the-floor refusal. Give-up codes
  propagate; none is folded into `-1`. A self-contained `rx_matchfn` accepts
  `ctx->ncap == 0, ctx->caps == NULL`.
- <a id="s2-p5"></a>[2¶5] **`rx_ctx.vars` / `nvars`** carry the caller's variable values for
  module `vars`, by name (`docs/spec/vars.md`); they are what keeps a
  var-bearing artifact's `<prefix>_match` an `rx_matchfn`.
- <a id="s2-p6"></a>[2¶6] **`rx_ctx.ncap`'s "watermark mid-match" reading has no producer.** Every
  emitted call site sets `ncap = 0` and nothing advances it, so no caller can
  observe a watermark; it is reserved for a future mid-match view.
- <a id="s2-p7"></a>[2¶7] **`rx_renderfn` carries a sizing protocol**: called with `out == NULL` and
  `outcap == 0` it writes nothing and returns the length it would produce.
  The typedef is in every artifact's block; a FUNCTION of this type is
  emitted only when a substitution template names one.
- <a id="s2-p8"></a>[2¶8] **`rx_group_entry`**: `slot` is the caps index the row delivers, or `-1`
  when this build delivers none; `ref` is NULL for the primary pattern's own
  groups and names the bound definition on a delivered row of a composed
  artifact (§5.5).
- <a id="s2-p9"></a>[2¶9] **`PCREC_ENGINE_DFA` / `PCREC_ENGINE_VM` are the only emitted names for
  `rx_info.engine`'s two values**; the compiler's internal engine enum is
  never emitted.
- <a id="s2-p10"></a>[2¶10] **Every macro in the block is unprefixed and identical under every
  prefix**, and is emitted even on an artifact that can never produce the
  value (a DFA-only artifact never returns a give-up code and never stamps a
  VM mask), so code written against the names compiles whichever engine a
  later compile selects.

<a id="s2-p11"></a>[2¶11] **`rx_info` is a struct TAG, not a typedef.** Every emitted reference spells
`struct rx_info`, and no bare `rx_info` type exists: under the default prefix
the per-artifact instance `<prefix>_info` is the identifier `rx_info`, which
a typedef of the same name could not coexist with. An embedder declares
`const struct rx_info *`; a consumer that wants a typedef'd name declares its
own, e.g. `typedef struct rx_info rx_info_t;`. This spelling is ruled (D57),
not provisional.

---

<a id="s3"></a>
## 3. Entry points

<a id="s3-p1"></a>[3¶1] Every artifact exports, unconditionally, these per-artifact symbols:

| symbol | what it is | section |
|---|---|---|
| `<prefix>_search` | leftmost-match search from a start position | §3.1 |
| `<prefix>_match` | anchored match-here, no captures; an `rx_matchfn` | §3.2 |
| `<prefix>_match_caps` | anchored match-here, delivering captures | §3.3 |
| `<prefix>_info` | the reflection structure (data, not a function) | §3.4, §6 |
| `<prefix>_next_pos` | the encoding residual: next character boundary | §3.1.1 |
| `<prefix>_valid_upto` | the subject validator | §3.1.2 |
| `<prefix>_search_in`, `<prefix>_match_in`, `<prefix>_match_caps_in` | the three above with caller-supplied working storage | §10 |

<a id="s3-p2"></a>[3¶2] Some artifacts also export and declare encoding-residual helpers the engine
calls across the residual seam: `<prefix>_span_match` /
`<prefix>_span_match_caseless` (a backreference- or variable-bearing
artifact; `docs/spec/vars.md` §7) and `<prefix>_var_valid` (a variable-bearing
artifact under a multi-byte encoding). They are not caller entries; their
signatures are not part of this contract.

<a id="s3-p3"></a>[3¶3] The parameter names used in this document (`s`, `n`, `startpos`, `caps`) are
expository; the emitted declarations spell them `subject`, `subject_length`,
`search_from` and `capture_spans`. A var-bearing artifact (module `vars`)
gives `<prefix>_search` and `<prefix>_search_in` a trailing
`const rx_var *vars, size_t nvars` pair, placed before `_search_in`'s buffer
descriptor, which stays last (`docs/spec/vars.md`); the `rx_ctx`-shaped
entries read the variables from `rx_ctx` and keep their signatures.

<a id="s3-p4"></a>[3¶4] **Which entry to call.** The discriminator is whether the start position is
KNOWN, never whether captures are wanted: `<prefix>_search` delivers full
captures when handed a `caps` buffer, so "first match plus its groups" is one
`<prefix>_search` call.

- <a id="s3-p5"></a>[3¶5] No start position known, with or without captures → `<prefix>_search`.
- <a id="s3-p6"></a>[3¶6] Start position known, captures wanted, no search → `<prefix>_match_caps`.
- <a id="s3-p7"></a>[3¶7] Start position known, neither offsets nor a search wanted → `<prefix>_match`.

<a id="s3-p8"></a>[3¶8] The un-suffixed entries `<prefix>_search`, `<prefix>_match` and
`<prefix>_match_caps` run on default working storage whose cost model is
§10.9 (the tiered default); a caller that supplies its own storage calls the
`_in` entries of §10.

<a id="s3-1"></a>
### 3.1 `<prefix>_search` — the search entry

```c
int <prefix>_search(const unsigned char *s, size_t n, size_t startpos,
                    ptrdiff_t (*caps)[2]);
```

<a id="s3-1-p1"></a>[3.1¶1] Searches `s[startpos..n)` for the leftmost match. Returns:

| return | meaning |
|---|---|
| `1` | match found; if `caps != NULL`, `<PREFIX>_NCAPS` pairs are written, `caps[0]` the whole-match span |
| `0` | no match; `caps` is left untouched |
| `PCREC_ERR_STEPS` / `_FRAMES` / `_WORK` / `_RECURSE` | the engine gave up (§4); `caps` untouched. `_RECURSE` has no producer |
| `PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL` | not a give-up (§4): the artifact detected its own analysis/emission inconsistency; `caps` untouched |
| `PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS` | not a give-up (§4): `startpos` is not a character boundary of the artifact's encoding, so the call is refused and nothing is attempted; `caps` untouched. Only an artifact compiled for an encoding with multi-byte characters, with the guard not denied, can return it (§9.2) |
| `PCREC_ERR_UNSET_VAR` | not a give-up (§4): a variable the pattern needs is unset or ill-formed (`docs/spec/vars.md`); `caps` untouched |
| `PCREC_ERR_UTF` | not a give-up (§4): a `-futf-check` artifact found an ill-formed sequence beginning in the checked range `[startpos − LB, n)`, so the call is refused before any attempt; `caps` untouched; `<prefix>_valid_upto(s, n, startpos)` is the offset (§9.4) |

- <a id="s3-1-p2"></a>[3.1¶2] **`0` means no match, not a zero-length match.** A zero-length match is a
  success: `1` with `caps[0][0] == caps[0][1]`. The anchored entries of
  §3.2/§3.3 use the other convention because their return carries a length:
  there `0` is a zero-length match and `-1` is no match.
- <a id="s3-1-p3"></a>[3.1¶3] **The return is not two-valued.** `if (<prefix>_search(…))` reads a
  give-up or a refusal as a match; test `== 1` for "matched".
- <a id="s3-1-p4"></a>[3.1¶4] **Every return other than `1` leaves the whole `caps` array untouched**, on
  every engine and through every entry that takes one (`_search`,
  `_search_in`, `_match_caps`, `_match_caps_in`). That includes a DFA artifact
  with `<PREFIX>_NCAPS >= 2` whose groups above 0 can never be set (each is
  reached only through a subroutine call, or sits under a `{0}`): those slots
  are written `PCREC_UNSET` on a success only (`tests/codegen/
  run_nomatch_caps.sh`).
- <a id="s3-1-p5"></a>[3.1¶5] **`caps` may be `NULL`** (an existence-only search).
- <a id="s3-1-p6"></a>[3.1¶6] **`startpos > n` returns `0`.** Every position at or beyond `n` counts as a
  character boundary.
- <a id="s3-1-p7"></a>[3.1¶7] **`^` anchors to absolute offset 0** regardless of `startpos`; **`\G`**
  asserts at `startpos` itself.
- <a id="s3-1-p8"></a>[3.1¶8] **`s` may be `NULL` only when `n == 0`.**

<a id="s3-1-p9"></a>[3.1¶9] **Every offset written to `caps` is an ABSOLUTE offset into `s`, never
relative to `startpos`.** Measured: searching `"xabcabcx"` for `abc` from
`startpos = 0` reports `[1,4)`, and the next search from `4` reports `[4,7)`.

<a id="s3-1-p10"></a>[3.1¶10] **A search may skip positions it proves cannot begin a match, and its answer
is the one a scan from `startpos` gives.**

- <a id="s3-1-p11"></a>[3.1¶11] It may begin its internal scan after `startpos` where a necessary literal
  proves no match begins earlier (`<PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF`, §6.3;
  `tuning.md` §2.41).
- <a id="s3-1-p12"></a>[3.1¶12] A prefilter-less VM artifact may skip a start position whose byte the
  pattern's start set excludes (`<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN`, §6.3;
  `tuning.md` §2.42).
- <a id="s3-1-p13"></a>[3.1¶13] Positions so proved consume no step budget and no capacity: the budgets
  meter only the work the matcher performs.
- <a id="s3-1-p14"></a>[3.1¶14] No artifact begins a scan later where that could change whether a
  budget-limited search answers or gives up (`tuning.md` §2.41: a
  count-collapsed prefilter declines the handoff).
- <a id="s3-1-p15"></a>[3.1¶15] A search that gives up under `-fno-start-set` — on steps, work, backtrack
  frames, trail, or a caller buffer's capacity — may return the answer an
  unbounded budget and capacity return when the skip is on. It never does the
  reverse: an answer under `-fno-start-set` is the answer with the skip.

<a id="s3-1-p16"></a>[3.1¶16] **`caps[0][0]` is where REPORTING begins, which is not always where matching
began.** `\K` resets the reported start to wherever the winning path last
crossed it (`docs/design/assertions_design.md` §6): on `a\Kb` over `"ab"` the
search consumes two bytes from offset 0 and reports `[1,2)`. Consequences,
all shared with PCRE2:

- <a id="s3-1-p17"></a>[3.1¶17] `caps[0][0]` can exceed the offset the match began at, so it is not a bound
  on where the engine looked.
- <a id="s3-1-p18"></a>[3.1¶18] `caps[0][0] == caps[0][1]` does not imply nothing was consumed: `ab\K` over
  `"ab"` reports `[2,2)` after consuming two bytes.
- <a id="s3-1-p19"></a>[3.1¶19] The anchored entries of §3.2/§3.3 return the CONSUMED length: on `ab\K` at
  `pos = 0` they return `2` while the span they report is `[2,2)`. That is
  what makes a callout's advance terminate.

<a id="s3-1-p20"></a>[3.1¶20] A pattern with no `\K` is unaffected. `\K` is module-gated (`assertions`) and
forces the VM engine.

<a id="s3-1-p21"></a>[3.1¶21] **A DFA search takes one of two forms, answer-identical and differing only in
cost and size** (`<PREFIX>_DFA_START`, §6.3; `tuning.md` §2.19). The
`"reverse-pass"` form runs a forward scan to find where the match ends and a
backwards scan over a second machine to find where it began. Where the
forward machine accepts before reading a byte (`a*`, `.*`, `[a-z]{0,4096}`
and their family), the compiler proves the start is `startpos` and emits
neither the backwards scan nor its machine: the `"pinned"` form. Both forms
write absolute offsets (the pinned form writes `caps[0][0] = startpos`) and
both keep the zero-length-match-is-a-success convention, on which the pinned
form depends. The observable difference is cost — roughly a factor of two on
a counted class run — and size. A pinned search at `startpos > 0` on a
machine whose start state depends on the preceding byte (`\b`, `(?m)^`) can
begin in a state from which nothing matches and returns `0`; the emitted
artifact keeps that test and marks it load-bearing.

<a id="s3-1-p22"></a>[3.1¶22] **The subject is `n` bytes and nothing more.** A `0x00` byte inside `s` is an
ordinary byte (only the PATTERN is NUL-terminated, §7), and the matcher never
reads `s[n]`: `s` need not be NUL-terminated and need not have a readable
byte after its end. Measured on both engines with the subject in an
exact-size heap allocation under AddressSanitizer: `a.b` and `a(.)b` both
match the 3 bytes `{'a', 0x00, 'b'}` (span `[0,3)`, group 1 `[1,2)`), and
matching, non-matching and `n == 0` searches over exact-size buffers are
clean; the same probe with `n` overstated by one fires a heap-buffer-overflow
at the matcher's own `memchr` prefilter. The DFA matcher writes
`caps[0][0]`/`caps[0][1]` only under `if (caps)`; an `--emit-main` driver
passes a real array, never `NULL`.

<a id="s3-1-p23"></a>[3.1¶23] Where a caller's `startpos` may point, and what happens on ill-formed text,
is §9.

<a id="s3-1-3"></a>
#### 3.1.3 Finding every match

<a id="s3-1-3-p1"></a>[3.1.3¶1] `<prefix>_search` is one-shot: it finds the first match at or after
`startpos`. There is no batch find-all primitive. A caller wanting every
match writes this loop:

```c
size_t p = 0;
while (p <= n) {
    int r = <prefix>_search(s, n, p, caps);
    if (r != 1) break;                       /* 0 = done; < 0 = gave up (§4) */
    report(caps[0][0], caps[0][1]);
    p = (caps[0][1] > caps[0][0])            /* non-empty: resume at its end, */
          ? <prefix>_next_pos(s, n, (size_t)caps[0][1] - 1)  /* boundary-aligned */
          : <prefix>_next_pos(s, n, (size_t)caps[0][0]);     /* EMPTY: next char */
}
```

- <a id="s3-1-3-p2"></a>[3.1.3¶2] **Restarting at the previous match's end is not enough**: it spins forever
  the first time a pattern matches empty (`a*` on `"bbb"` returns `[0,0)`
  from `startpos = 0` for ever).
- <a id="s3-1-3-p3"></a>[3.1.3¶3] **The empty-match advance.** A zero-length match is reported like any other,
  and the next search starts at the next CHARACTER boundary past its START,
  `caps[0][0]` — not past the loop variable, since an empty match can be
  found later than the position searched from (and `\K` makes that routine).
- <a id="s3-1-3-p4"></a>[3.1.3¶4] **The non-empty advance is aligned.** After a non-empty match the next
  search starts at `<prefix>_next_pos(s, n, end - 1)`, the first boundary at
  or after `end`. On a well-formed subject that is `end` itself, under `byte`
  and `utf8` alike. It differs only where the match ends immediately before a
  STRAY continuation byte: there the loop steps over it to the next
  non-continuation byte rather than handing the engine a `startpos` the
  boundary guard refuses (measured: `a` over `a\x80a` under `-e utf8` finds 2
  matches, as libpcre2 with `PCRE2_MATCH_INVALID_UTF` through the same loop
  does). `end - 1` cannot underflow (a non-empty match has `end >= 1`), and
  `end - 1 < n` keeps `<prefix>_next_pos` in its boundary-skipping domain.
- <a id="s3-1-3-p5"></a>[3.1.3¶5] **Termination.** `p` moves strictly forward every iteration
  (`<prefix>_next_pos` returns a position strictly greater than its
  argument), and `p > n` ends the loop.
- <a id="s3-1-3-p6"></a>[3.1.3¶6] **The loop never triggers a boundary refusal.** Every position it computes
  — `0`, an aligned match end, a `<prefix>_next_pos` advance — is a boundary,
  on a well-formed subject or an ill-formed one, so a caller who writes it as
  shown never sees `PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS` from it. A continuation byte is never
  a match START (§9.5), so stepping over one cannot lose a match. (The
  empty-match family at an ill-formed subject END is `docs/dev/
  known_issues.md` K74.)
- <a id="s3-1-3-p7"></a>[3.1.3¶7] **Do not inline `+ 1` in place of `<prefix>_next_pos`.** The loop as written
  is final for every encoding: compiled against a `-e utf8` artifact it
  advances by characters with no source change.

<a id="s3-1-3-p8"></a>[3.1.3¶8] **Measured.** The loop, compiled against real artifacts on both engines
(captures-on and `--no-captures`), agrees span for span with
`python3 re.finditer` on 22 of the 26 `byte`-encoded pairs in
`tests/encseam/findall_cases.txt` (run in `make test`): `a*` over `"bbb"` →
`(0,0) (1,1) (2,2) (3,3)`, `x?y` over `"yy"` → `(0,1) (1,2)`, `a|` over
`"bab"` → `(0,0) (1,2) (2,2) (3,3)`, `a|b*` over `"cbbac"` →
`(0,0) (1,3) (3,4) (4,4) (5,5)`, and `a*`/`"aaa"`, `a?`/`"aba"`,
`b*`/`"abbbab"`, `(a|)`/`"xax"`, `a(b|)c`/`"acabc"`, `(ab)*`/`"ababx"`,
`a{0,2}`/`"aaaa"`, `[a-c]*`/`"xabcx"`, `[0-9]+`/`"a12b345"`, `a{2,}`/`"aaaa"`,
`(?:ab|a)`/`"aab"`, `(a*)*`/`"aab"`, `.`/`"abc"`, `ab$`/`"xabab"`,
`^a`/`"aa"`, `c*` and `x` over the empty subject, and `a`/`"a"`; the other
four are the lossy class below. The ill-formed-subject witnesses are
`tests/rxtsource/fixtures/mc_illformed_utf8.rxtin`.

<a id="s3-1-3-p9"></a>[3.1.3¶9] **Where the loop is lossy.** It reports FEWER matches than PCRE2 and python
`re` for a pattern that PREFERS the empty match at a position where a
non-empty match also starts. Those engines, after an empty match at `p`,
retry at `p` with "empty not permitted here" (`PCRE2_NOTEMPTY_ATSTART`) and
report the non-empty match too. No pcrec entry can express that retry, so the
advance rule above is the whole of what a pcrec consumer can do. The
divergence is always an OMISSION — the loop's spans are a strict subset of
`re.finditer`'s, which the suite checks: `|a` over `"aaa"` gives 4 spans
`(0,0) (1,1) (2,2) (3,3)` where `re.finditer` gives 7; likewise `a*?` over
`"aaa"` (4 vs 7), `a??` over `"aba"` (4 vs 6) and `b*?` over `"abba"`
(5 vs 7). A pattern whose preference picks a non-empty match wherever one
starts — every greedy quantifier among the agreeing cases — does not diverge.

<a id="s3-1-3-p10"></a>[3.1.3¶10] **`\G` under the loop means "contiguous with the previous match"** —
PCRE2's global-iteration semantics, because the loop passes its resume
position as `startpos` and `\G` asserts there (`docs/design/
assertions_design.md` §4.3). `\G\w+` is a TOKENIZER: it reports `(0,2)` on
`"ab ab ab"` and stops at the first gap, where `\w+` reports all three
(`tests/assertions/run_gstart_diff.sh` §1, against libpcre2 driven through the
same loop).

<a id="s3-1-3-p11"></a>[3.1.3¶11] **`\K` under the loop is safe.** The loop advances off `caps[0][1]`, which
`\K` does not move. A `\K` pattern can report an empty span after consuming
bytes and then takes the EMPTY arm, advancing one character from the
reported start: `ab\K` over `"ababab"` reports `2,2 6,6` (the match at 2..4
is not reported again at 4) and `a\Kb` over `"ababab"` reports `1,2 3,4 5,6`,
both identical to libpcre2 driven through the same loop
(`tests/assertions/run_kreset_diff.sh` §5).

<a id="s3-1-1"></a>
#### 3.1.1 `<prefix>_next_pos` — the encoding residual

```c
size_t <prefix>_next_pos(const unsigned char *s, size_t n, size_t pos);
```

<a id="s3-1-1-p1"></a>[3.1.1¶1] Returns the smallest position STRICTLY GREATER than `pos` that is a character
boundary of the artifact's encoding, counting every position `>= n` as a
boundary: the result is in `(pos, n]` when `pos < n`, and `pos + 1` when
`pos >= n`. It is the one place an artifact's byte-vs-character distinction
lives (D58; `docs/dev/plan.md` `[DD-12]`).

- <a id="s3-1-1-p2"></a>[3.1.1¶2] **An ordinary extern function**, declared where the other entries are
  declared (the `.h`, or the self-contained `.c`) and defined in the `.c`;
  not a macro, not `static inline`.
- <a id="s3-1-1-p3"></a>[3.1.1¶3] **It reads `s` only at offsets in `[pos, n)`**, so the `(s == NULL, n == 0)`
  subject `<prefix>_search` accepts is legal here; under `byte` it does not
  read `s` at all.
- <a id="s3-1-1-p4"></a>[3.1.1¶4] **`pos > n` is not an error**: the result is `pos + 1`.
- <a id="s3-1-1-p5"></a>[3.1.1¶5] **The result is always strictly greater than `pos`.**
- <a id="s3-1-1-p6"></a>[3.1.1¶6] **It is never called from the artifact's own engine.** The hot path does
  not depend on the encoding (DD-12 (7)); `tests/codegen/
  run_codegen_tests.sh` checks every emitted engine body for a residual
  reference across six emission shapes in both artifact forms, and
  `tests/mech/sabotages/S68_residual_in_hot_loop.sh` validates the check
  (under `byte` a residual call in a hot loop computes the same value, so only
  the structural check can see one).
- <a id="s3-1-1-p7"></a>[3.1.1¶7] **One encoding per artifact.** An artifact embeds exactly one encoding's
  residual block, chosen per compile call by `pcrec_options.encoding` (§8.2,
  §9.1), so differently-prefixed artifacts compiled for different encodings
  compose in one translation unit.

<a id="s3-1-1-p8"></a>[3.1.1¶8] Under `byte` the body is `pos + 1`. Verbatim from a `-p rx -fcomments` build of
`'a(b|c)+d'`:

```c
/* byte encoding: one byte is one character, so the next boundary after pos
 * is pos + 1 and the subject is never read. */
size_t rx_next_pos(const unsigned char *s, size_t n, size_t pos)
{
    (void)s; (void)n;
    return pos + 1;
}
```

<a id="s3-1-1-p9"></a>[3.1.1¶9] **Under `utf8` the advance is defined on every input, well-formed or not, and
this rule is normative:**

> <a id="s3-1-1-p10"></a>[3.1.1¶10] **From `pos + 1`, advance past every byte in the range `0x80`-`0xBF`,
> stopping at the first byte outside that range or at `n`.**

<a id="s3-1-1-p11"></a>[3.1.1¶11] A well-formed character is skipped whole; an ill-formed sequence degrades to
the next non-continuation byte rather than to a position inside the garbage;
the loop is bounded by `n` rather than by a character's maximum of three
continuation bytes, which makes the degradation total. The same rule is the
engine's own retry advance (K49), and `rxt_format.md` §1.7's `mc`
production states it for a foreign consumer. Verbatim from a
`-e utf8 -fcomments` artifact:

```c
/* utf8 encoding: skip forward over continuation bytes. A well-formed
 * character's continuations are at most 3, but the loop is bounded by n
 * rather than by 4 so that ill-formed input degrades to "next
 * non-continuation byte" instead of to a mid-garbage position. */
size_t rx_next_pos(const unsigned char *s, size_t n, size_t pos)
{
    size_t i = pos + 1;
    while (i < n && (s[i] & 0xC0) == 0x80) i++;
    return i;
}
```

<a id="s3-1-2"></a>
#### 3.1.2 `<prefix>_valid_upto` — the subject validator

```c
size_t <prefix>_valid_upto(const unsigned char *s, size_t n, size_t startpos);
```

<a id="s3-1-2-p1"></a>[3.1.2¶1] Returns the offset of the FIRST BYTE of the first ill-formed sequence of the
artifact's encoding that begins at or after `f`, where `f` is `startpos`
stepped back LB characters by PCRE2's raw walk (§9.4) — or `n` when there is
none, and `n` when `startpos > n`. The first byte is the sequence's lead, or a
stray continuation byte itself. That is `PCRE2_UTF`'s own error offset
(`pcre2_get_startchar`) on every measured kind: truncated, overlong,
surrogate, above U+10FFFF, `0xF5`-`0xFF`, isolated continuation
(`docs/design/utf_valid_design.md` §1, libpcre2 10.46).

- <a id="s3-1-2-p2"></a>[3.1.2¶2] **Every artifact exports it, whatever `-futf-check` says** (D133 Q4). Under
  `byte` the body is `return n;` and `s` is never read, so the
  `(s == NULL, n == 0)` subject is legal and a caller's code compiles
  unchanged across encodings.
- <a id="s3-1-2-p3"></a>[3.1.2¶3] **A `-futf-check` artifact refuses exactly the calls for which this returns
  `< n`, and the return is the offset of that refusal**: pass the same
  `startpos` the refused call was given (under `-fstartpos-guard=align`, the
  aligned one). The step-back happens inside the entry, so an error inside the
  lookbehind window before `startpos` is reported.
- <a id="s3-1-2-p4"></a>[3.1.2¶4] **It is called once per call from the entries, never from an engine body**
  (DD-12 (7); the residual check counts its call sites as it does
  `<prefix>_next_pos`'s). LB reaches the body as `<prefix>_VALID_LB`, a
  `.c`-only macro that is not otherwise part of this contract.
- <a id="s3-1-2-p5"></a>[3.1.2¶5] **A mid-character `startpos` is not refused here**: with LB 0 the walk starts
  ON the continuation byte, which is then reported as ill-formed. The checking
  entries never ask that question, because the boundary guard (or the
  alignment) runs first.

<a id="s3-1-2-p6"></a>[3.1.2¶6] **Find-all under the check: validate once, loop on the default artifact**
(D133 Q6). A find-all loop over a `-futf-check` artifact validates `[f, n)`
on every call, so `m` matches cost O(n·m) validation bytes (PCRE2 documents
`PCRE2_NO_UTF_CHECK` for the same property). The linear idiom needs one
artifact compiled WITHOUT `-futf-check`:

```c
if (<prefix>_valid_upto(s, n, 0) != n) { /* refuse: offset is the return */ }
else { /* run the §3.1 loop on this same artifact, unchanged */ }
```

<a id="s3-1-2-p7"></a>[3.1.2¶7] It answers exactly as the checking artifact would on every call of the loop,
because every call's checked range lies inside `[0, n)`. No validity cursor is
kept inside the artifact across calls (§5.3 forbids the state). The per-call
"check as you move forward" contract (`-futf-check=extent`) is reserved and
refused (`docs/design/utf_valid_design.md` §2.2/§2.4).

<a id="s3-2"></a>
### 3.2 `<prefix>_match` — the anchored match-here entry

```c
ptrdiff_t <prefix>_match(const rx_ctx *ctx);   /* an rx_matchfn, §2 */
```

<a id="s3-2-p1"></a>[3.2¶1] **Matches at exactly `ctx->pos`; a match starting anywhere else is not
reported.** That is the contract; how an artifact achieves it is not.

<a id="s3-2-p2"></a>[3.2¶2] Returns the matched length (`>= 0`; `0` is a zero-length match at
`ctx->pos`), `-1` on no match, a give-up code (§4), or one of §3.1's caller
refusals at `ctx->pos`: `PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS`, `PCREC_ERR_UNSET_VAR`, and under
`-futf-check` `PCREC_ERR_UTF`, from the same checks at the same position, in
the same order (the boundary guard first) and over the same checked range
`<prefix>_search` uses. Under `-fstartpos-guard=align` a misaligned
`ctx->pos` answers `-1` (no match begins inside a character), after the check
has run from the aligned position. On a subject that BEGINS with continuation
bytes it answers `-1` at `ctx->pos == 0` (§9.3), and `ctx->pos > ctx->len`
answers `-1`.

<a id="s3-2-p3"></a>[3.2¶3] It delivers **no captures**: `ctx->caps` is an input (§5), not an output
channel. A top-level caller passes `ctx->ncap = 0, ctx->caps = NULL`, which
every `rx_matchfn` accepts.

<a id="s3-2-p4"></a>[3.2¶4] **A DFA artifact's `<prefix>_match` takes one of two forms**, named by
`<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH` and `rx_info.match_form` (§6.3); both give the same
answers. A VM artifact's `<prefix>_match` is the VM's own anchored body, with
no search loop.

- <a id="s3-2-p5"></a>[3.2¶5] **`"unwrapped"`**: the artifact carries a third machine — the forward
  tables without the start-anywhere self-loop — and runs it forward from
  `ctx->pos`. A failing probe stops at the first byte that cannot continue a
  match beginning there; a succeeding one costs one forward scan
  (`docs/design/anchored_match_unwrapped.md` §3 argues the reported length
  equals the other form's on every input).
- <a id="s3-2-p6"></a>[3.2¶6] **`"search-filter"`**: the entry runs the artifact's unanchored search and
  rejects any match whose start is not `ctx->pos`. On a FAILING match-here the
  underlying search may skim the rest of the subject for a later match the
  filter then discards (the state-0 `memchr` skip keeps it a skim), so a
  caller issuing many expected-to-fail probes against long subjects is in
  this form's worst case and can read the form off the artifact. Four
  populations take it: `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN "attempt"` (a `^`- or `\G`-bearing
  pattern), an anchored machine
  that exceeded a DFA cap (a selection outcome, never a refusal), any build
  under `-fno-anchored-dfa` (`tuning.md` §2.15), and an artifact whose anchored
  machine was dropped to fit an emitted-size cap (`limits.md` §8, "The
  optional-contributor drop") — the only one of the four where a size limit
  rather than the pattern's shape cost the faster form. It is identified by
  `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "size-cap-retry"`, and raising `--max-emit-bytes` gets
  the anchored machine back.
- <a id="s3-2-p6a"></a>[3.2¶6a] **`"nomatch"`**: the artifact matches nothing
  (`<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN "empty"`), so the entry answers `-1` without a scan,
  after the startpos check every match-here entry makes (§3.1).

<a id="s3-3"></a>
### 3.3 `<prefix>_match_caps` — the anchored, capture-delivering entry

```c
ptrdiff_t <prefix>_match_caps(const rx_ctx *ctx, ptrdiff_t (*caps_out)[2]);
```

<a id="s3-3-p1"></a>[3.3¶1] The anchoring promise, return space and forms of `<prefix>_match` (§3.2),
plus captures. On success `caps_out[0..<PREFIX>_NCAPS-1]` are all written,
`caps_out[0]` is `[ctx->pos, ctx->pos + length)` (under `"unwrapped"` the entry
delegates to `<prefix>_match` and fills that span itself), and **`caps_out[k]`
is capturing group `k`** for `k >= 1`, in the pattern's own left-to-right
numbering, on any captures-on build: for the primary pattern's own groups
`slot == number` is permanent (D61; §5.4/§5.5 for rows that deliver
elsewhere).

<a id="s3-3-p2"></a>[3.3¶2] **On every negative return `caps_out` is untouched, give-ups included.**
`ctx->caps` / `ctx->ncap` are read as ordinary `rx_ctx` input, unrelated to
`caps_out`; a top-level call passes `ncap = 0, caps = NULL`.

<a id="s3-4"></a>
### 3.4 `<prefix>_info` — the reflection structure

```c
extern const struct rx_info <prefix>_info;
```

<a id="s3-4-p1"></a>[3.4¶1] One instance per artifact, link-time constant data with no constructor and no
run-time initializer. §6 lists its fields and §6.1 its section placement.

<a id="s3-5"></a>
### 3.5 Give-ups across the entries

<a id="s3-5-p1"></a>[3.5¶1] **Every entry propagates the give-up codes unchanged; none is collapsed to
`-1`.** `<prefix>_match` and `<prefix>_match_caps` return the same code
`<prefix>_search` would for the same work, on both engines (D49; the DFA
wrapper returns `found` when `found < 0`, and the VM entry returns its body's
result with no translation). A caller that tests only `r < 0` is unaffected;
one doing an exact `== -1` comparison sees give-ups as distinct values. A DFA
artifact never returns a give-up code — it has no counter to exhaust — but
its entries are written to propagate one, and every artifact defines the
constants, so a caller's `switch` survives a later compile selecting the VM.

<a id="s3-5-p2"></a>[3.5¶2] **WHICH entry gives up on a given input is a property of that entry**, because
the entries do different amounts of work, and it goes both ways. Measured on
`(a|aa)+b`: built `--step-budget=3`, over `"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaX"`
`<prefix>_search` returns `0` (its DFA prefilter answers without entering the
VM) while `<prefix>_match` and `<prefix>_match_caps` return `-2`; built
`--backtrack-frames=1`, over `"xxaaaaab"` `<prefix>_search` returns `-3` while
both anchored entries return `-1` (anchoring at 0 fails at once and spends no
frame), and over `"ab"` all three return `-3`. A caller handles give-ups on
whichever entry it calls, and never infers from one entry's clean answer that
another would give one.

<a id="s3-5-p3"></a>[3.5¶3] **The DFA wrappers' local caps arrays are zero-initialized** (`= {{0}}`), in
`<prefix>_match`, `<prefix>_match_caps` and the `--emit-main` `main()`. When a
pattern's DFA is a single dead state, `<prefix>_search` always returns 0, gcc
`-O1` inlines it and reports the array maybe-uninitialized though the read is
unreachable; the initializer keeps a consumer's `-Werror` build clean
(`docs/dev/known_issues.md` K28). It is never observed and changes no answer;
restructuring the test instead was measured not to silence the report.

<a id="s3-6"></a>
### 3.6 Whole-subject and end-anchored matching: the `(?:P)\z` idiom

<a id="s3-6-p1"></a>[3.6¶1] There is no end-anchored entry: §3.1–§3.3 answer "does a match start here",
never "does a match cover here to `n`". A caller wanting PCRE2's
`PCRE2_ANCHORED|PCRE2_ENDANCHORED` regime compiles `(?:P)\z` — the pattern
`P` in a non-capturing group, followed by `\z` — and calls any entry as usual.
The idiom is permanent (`docs/dev/decisions.md` D77, plan row `[OS-4]`): no
end-anchored generation axis is built, and one is built only under a
measurement that justifies it. A caller asking both questions compiles two
artifacts; any optimization of `\z` benefits the idiom exactly as it benefits
every other `\z`-bearing pattern.

- <a id="s3-6-p2"></a>[3.6¶2] **`\z`, not `$`.** `$` admits a trailing newline at default options:
  `(?:foo)$` matches `"foo\n"` at `[0,3)`, while `(?:foo)\z` on the same
  subject does not match. `\z` (module `assertions`) admits nothing after it;
  of `$`, `\Z` and `\z` it is the only anchor with that property at default
  options.
- <a id="s3-6-p3"></a>[3.6¶3] **Testing `length == n` on the ordinary anchored entry is not a
  substitute.** It is sufficient but not necessary, because leftmost-first
  preference picks the first alternative that matches, not the longest:
  `a|ab` anchored over `"ab"` reports `[0,1)`, so `length == n` says no, while
  `(?:a|ab)\z` over `"ab"` reports `[0,2)` — `\z` forces the engine past the
  `a` branch into `ab`.
- <a id="s3-6-p4"></a>[3.6¶4] **The idiom's cost.** A `\z` pattern still selects the DFA, and its
  `<prefix>_match` runs the artifact's own anchored machine (§3.2
  `"unwrapped"`). Measured over the comparative bench's 85 compliance
  subjects: the matching split is 1.031× the backtracking VM's time and short
  valid emails 0.482× (`docs/design/anchored_match_unwrapped.md` §7.1).
- <a id="s3-6-p5"></a>[3.6¶5] **Its stamps** (§6.3): `(?:foo|bar)\z` stamps `RX_DFA_SCAN "unanchored"` (the
  idiom anchors only the end) and `RX_DFA_PREFILTER "byte-class-bounded"`;
  `(?:foo)\z` stamps `"memchr-bounded"`. `RX_DFA_SCAN "attempt"` comes from a
  leading `^`/`\A`, which the idiom does not add.

---

<a id="s4"></a>
## 4. Give-up and refusal codes

<a id="s4-p1"></a>[4¶1] The negative returns below `-1` form one code space (D49), with the same value
meaning the same thing at every entry: `<prefix>_search`, every `rx_matchfn`
(hence `<prefix>_match` and any callout), `<prefix>_match_caps`, and the three
`_in` entries. Uniformity is about the codes, not about when a give-up happens
(§3.5). The constants are in the shared ABI block on every artifact (§2):

| code | value | class | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PCREC_ERR_STEPS` | −2 | give-up | the step budget (backtrack resumptions) ran out |
| `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` | −3 | give-up | a backtracking capacity ran out (below) |
| `PCREC_ERR_WORK` | −4 | give-up | the work budget (forward work the fail label never sees) ran out |
| `PCREC_ERR_RECURSE` | −5 | give-up | reserved; no emitter returns it |
| `PCREC_ERR_FLOOR` | −5 | — | the partition: give-ups are `[PCREC_ERR_FLOOR, -2]` |
| `PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL` | −6 | below the floor | the artifact detected its own inconsistency |
| `PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS` | −7 | below the floor | refused: the caller's `startpos` / `ctx->pos` is not a character boundary |
| `PCREC_ERR_UNSET_VAR` | −8 | below the floor | refused: an unset or ill-formed variable value (`docs/spec/vars.md`) |
| `PCREC_ERR_UTF` | −9 | below the floor | refused: `-futf-check` found an ill-formed subject |

<a id="s4-p2"></a>[4¶2] **Give-ups**, `[PCREC_ERR_FLOOR, -2]`, say the engine ran and exhausted a
resource. A DFA artifact has no counter and never returns one, though it
defines them and its `--emit-main` driver carries the full handler text for
them. `PCREC_ERR_RECURSE` is reserved for a recursion-depth counter that the
default artifact does not carry (D71 item 1: a future diagnostic generation
axis, not a runtime flag); it is as unreachable on every artifact as
`PCREC_ERR_STEPS` is on a DFA-only one.

<a id="s4-p3"></a>[4¶3] **`PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` names a RESOURCE, not an array and not an owner.** The
resume stack (`<PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAMES`) and its undo trail
(`<PREFIX>_TRAIL_FRAMES`) both report it, and which one ran out is not
reported: measured on `^(a(?1)?b)$`, the artifact gives up with the trail full
and two thirds of its resume stack unused (`docs/design/
frame_buffer_design.md` §4). The same code, with the same meaning, covers a
caller-supplied buffer (§10.3), and there too it does not say whose buffer it
was. From an un-suffixed entry it always means the stamped default ran out,
never the fast tier (§10.9).

<a id="s4-p4"></a>[4¶4] **One call to an un-suffixed entry may spend up to twice the step budget and
twice the work budget.** The tiered default (§10.9) re-runs a match on the
full default storage after a `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` give-up on its fast tier, with
both budgets refilled. A returned `PCREC_ERR_STEPS` still means one attempt
exhausted a full budget. The `_in` entries have no tier and are bounded by one
budget; a caller needing a hard bound on one call's work uses `_in` or
`-fno-tiered-entry` (`tuning.md` §2.12).

<a id="s4-p5"></a>[4¶5] **Below the floor: not give-ups.** Values strictly below `PCREC_ERR_FLOOR` are
reserved for abort and refusal semantics. Every artifact defines all four
codes; each is returnable only where its cause can exist, and the constants
are emitted regardless so that a caller's `switch` survives a later compile
under a different encoding or engine. None renumbers the give-up partition.

- <a id="s4-p6"></a>[4¶6] **`PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL`** — the artifact caught its own inconsistency: a
  compile-time width analysis (`pcrec_maxw`) disagreeing with what the
  emitter walked, never a run-time resource give-up. Its one producer is
  module `lookaround`'s negative-polarity lookbehind end-check (`(?<!X)`),
  where a declined branch is the assertion SUCCEEDING, so a width
  disagreement would be a false match; the check is redundant for the width
  class the module ships and is emitted as a self-consistency guard. A
  top-level entry propagates it to its caller like any negative return.
- <a id="s4-p7"></a>[4¶7] **`PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS`** — a refusal of the CALL: the caller named a
  `startpos` (or `ctx->pos`) that is not a character boundary, so nothing was
  attempted and no budget was touched (§9.2). Unreachable under `byte`, where
  no guard is emitted.
- <a id="s4-p8"></a>[4¶8] **`PCREC_ERR_UNSET_VAR`** — a refusal of the call: a variable value the
  pattern needs is unset, or ill-formed under a multi-byte encoding; nothing
  attempted, `caps` untouched (`docs/spec/vars.md`).
- <a id="s4-p9"></a>[4¶9] **`PCREC_ERR_UTF`** — a refusal of the call: a `-futf-check` artifact found
  an ill-formed sequence beginning in `[startpos − LB, n)`, before any attempt
  (§9.4); `caps` untouched; `<prefix>_valid_upto(s, n, startpos)` is the
  offset. One code covers every kind of ill-formedness (D26: pcrec owes the
  refusal and the offset, not PCRE2's twenty `PCRE2_ERROR_UTF8_*` values).
  Only a `-futf-check` artifact under an encoding with ill-formed byte strings
  can return it.

<a id="s4-p10"></a>[4¶10] **Composed call sites trap below the floor, except on `PCREC_ERR_UTF`.** A
generated call site that invokes another `rx_matchfn` (a callout, a composed
submatcher) must enforce

```c
if (ret < PCREC_ERR_FLOOR && ret != PCREC_ERR_UTF) __builtin_trap();
```

and return a `PCREC_ERR_UTF` outward unchanged (D133 Q11). The rule binds
call sites that call INTO another matcher, not an exported entry's own
`return`. `PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL` and `PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS` at a composed callee
mean the engine broke its own rule (every position an engine generates is a
boundary, §9.5), so trapping is the design; `PCREC_ERR_UTF` is caused by the
caller's data — a checking callee whose LB reaches before the outer call's
range can legitimately refuse it. pcrec emits no such call site today; the
obligation binds the first that does.

<a id="s4-p11"></a>[4¶11] **Where the numbers live.** This section states what each value means. The
numeric defaults and overrides of the step and work budgets and the frame and
trail capacities, the compile-time state-count ceilings, the emitted-size caps
and their retry ladder, the tiered entry's numbers, and the K33/K34
documented-divergence detail are `docs/spec/limits.md`'s (§3, §5, §8); the
`pcrec_options` fields that override them are §8.2's.

---

<a id="s5"></a>
## 5. Captures and groups

```c
const ptrdiff_t (*caps)[2];         /* rx_ctx field; half-open [start, end) pairs */
#define <PREFIX>_NCAPS <n>          /* per-artifact, compile-time constant */
#define PCREC_UNSET ((ptrdiff_t)-1) /* contract constant, shared block (§2) */
```

- <a id="s5-p1"></a>[5¶1] **Unset is `{-1, -1}`** in both slots of a pair; `caps[k][0] < 0` is a
  sufficient unset test.
- <a id="s5-p2"></a>[5¶2] **Index 0 is always the whole match**, so `<PREFIX>_NCAPS >= 1`.
- <a id="s5-p3"></a>[5¶3] **`<PREFIX>_NCAPS` is a property of the ARTIFACT, not of the pattern text.**
  A DFA artifact always has `<PREFIX>_NCAPS 1`, capture-bearing pattern or
  not, so `<PREFIX>_NCAPS > 1` implies the VM engine. `'a(b|c)+d'` compiled
  `--no-captures` emits `RX_NCAPS 1` with `rx_info.ngroups == 1`; compiled
  with captures on (the default) it emits `RX_NCAPS 2`. `rx_info.ncaps ==
  <PREFIX>_NCAPS` always.
- <a id="s5-p4"></a>[5¶4] **Every pair `0..<PREFIX>_NCAPS-1` is written on a completed match**; no
  watermark is needed at read time.
- <a id="s5-p5"></a>[5¶5] **On a failed match the caller's array is left untouched**, and a give-up or
  a refusal is a failure for this rule: every negative return from an
  anchored entry, and a `0` or negative return from `<prefix>_search`, leaves
  the array as the caller left it. The return value alone communicates
  failure.
- <a id="s5-p6"></a>[5¶6] **Caller-owned, fixed-size, compile-time-sized**: a caller declares
  `ptrdiff_t caps[<PREFIX>_NCAPS][2];` on the stack. Nothing in the match
  contract allocates.
- <a id="s5-p7"></a>[5¶7] **`ctx->caps` handed to a callout mid-match is valid for that one call
  only**; the engine rewrites the storage afterwards (trail-based undo). A
  callout that keeps the pointer and reads it later has a bug of its own.
- <a id="s5-p8"></a>[5¶8] **A completed match's `caps` are stable until the next match call reusing
  the same buffer**; the matcher never overwrites a buffer mid-splice.
- <a id="s5-p9"></a>[5¶9] **`caps[k]` is group `k`** for the primary pattern's own groups on a
  captures-on build (§3.3; D61's permanent prefix, §6
  [`ngroups`](#s6-p3)).

<a id="s5-1"></a>
### 5.1 What a written slot holds

<a id="s5-1-p1"></a>[5.1¶1] Two rules govern which value a group inside a repeated construct holds,
measured three-way unanimous (python `re`, libpcre2 and pcrec agree):

1. <a id="s5-1-p2"></a>[5.1¶2] **Cross-iteration retention.** A group inside a quantifier whose
   subexpression did not run in the FINAL iteration keeps its value from the
   last iteration in which it did run. `((a)|(b))*` over `"ab"` reports group
   2 as `[0,1)`. Unset means "never participated in the whole match".
2. <a id="s5-1-p3"></a>[5.1¶3] **An empty final iteration still overwrites.** `(a*)*` and `(a?)*` over
   `"aaa"` both report group 1 as `[3,3)`.

<a id="s5-1-p4"></a>[5.1¶4] After a successful match a slot holds the group's last-executed span or is
genuinely unset; a caller never reasons about which iteration produced it.

<a id="s5-2"></a>
### 5.2 Explicit non-requirements

<a id="s5-2-p1"></a>[5.2¶1] Deliberately not part of the MATCH-path contract (the compile path does
allocate; its lifecycle is §8's `pcrec_output` / `pcrec_output_free`):

- <a id="s5-2-p2"></a>[5.2¶2] No ovector sizing negotiation — the group count is a compile-time fact.
- <a id="s5-2-p3"></a>[5.2¶3] No match-data object, no allocation, no lifecycle to manage.
- <a id="s5-2-p4"></a>[5.2¶4] No run-time "does group N exist" query.
- <a id="s5-2-p5"></a>[5.2¶5] No run-time name lookup for template resolution (a future substitution
  compiler resolves `${name}` at pcrec-compile time).
- <a id="s5-2-p6"></a>[5.2¶6] No partial-match or streaming window state.
- <a id="s5-2-p7"></a>[5.2¶7] No callout context beyond what `rx_ctx` carries: a binding's `user` data
  lives in its `rx_callout_ref`, and nothing about WHICH callout is firing is
  visible to `rx_matchfn`'s signature.

<a id="s5-3"></a>
### 5.3 Concurrency and reentrancy

<a id="s5-3-p1"></a>[5.3¶1] **A generated matcher holds no mutable state of its own.** Every entry's
working state lives in its own stack frame, in the caller's `caps` buffer, or
in a caller-supplied buffer (§10); the tables, bitmaps and the `rx_info`
instance are `const`. Therefore:

- <a id="s5-3-p2"></a>[5.3¶2] Any number of threads may call the same artifact's entries concurrently,
  **provided each call has its own `caps`/`caps_out` buffer and, for an `_in`
  entry, its own frame and trail buffers.** Sharing either between concurrent
  calls is a data race in the CALLER's code; the matcher does not serialize
  it.
- <a id="s5-3-p3"></a>[5.3¶3] The same holds for one thread re-entering a matcher (from a callout), with
  the same distinct-buffer rule: the inner call needs its own storage.
- <a id="s5-3-p4"></a>[5.3¶4] `<prefix>_info` is read-only and may be read from anywhere at any time.
- <a id="s5-3-p5"></a>[5.3¶5] There is no way to set a buffer once per artifact or per thread: that would
  be mutable emitted state (which this section forbids and TS-1 rejects) or a
  thread-local (which fails reentrancy). The buffer travels with the call.

<a id="s5-3-p6"></a>[5.3¶6] **This binds future emitters**: an engine that wanted mutable scratch state
would have to change this section first.

<a id="s5-3-p7"></a>[5.3¶7] **The promise is collectable only with enough stack headroom at the call
site.** An artifact whose frame requirement is not statically bounded keeps
its default backtracking storage in a non-inlined internal function that only
a `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` escalation reaches (§10.9). Measured on a `-p rx
--features all` build of `^(a(?1)?b)$`: `<prefix>_search`'s own frame is
3,184 bytes and the internal function's 131,216, so a call needs 134,400 bytes
of free stack at the call site to be safe on every subject (`limits.md` §5
states the rule). A call's frame lands wherever the stack pointer already is,
so a thread's nominal size equals the headroom only at call depth ~0. At depth
~0 on a musl-default 128 KB thread that artifact matches every subject the fast
tier holds and faults on one deep enough to escalate; a glibc-default 8 MB main
thread is unaffected, and a statically bounded pattern pays nothing extra
(`a(b|c)+d`'s entry frame is 208 bytes). Which subjects escalate depends on
pattern and subject, not on anything a caller can bound in advance. **The
remedy is the `_in` entries** (§10): their own frame measures 144 bytes at
`-O2` (312 with the two statics they call through, 224 at `-O3`), and the
default storage never reaches them. A caller that cannot supply storage sizes
the thread for the artifact or compiles with a smaller `--backtrack-frames`.
The default path is unchanged by design (D73 keeps the stamped 2048/3072
default); `docs/dev/known_issues.md` K33 carries the limitation and
`tests/thread/run_stackdepth_tests.sh` reproduces both halves: the small entry
frame, the deep tier dying on a 128 KB thread, and `<prefix>_search_in`
matching the same subject on the same thread.

<a id="s5-3-p8"></a>[5.3¶8] **Guarded by shipped checks in `make test`:**

- <a id="s5-3-p9"></a>[5.3¶9] **TS-1** (D19), static: scans every emitted file across nine emission shapes
  and fails on any non-const static object or any reference to a non-reentrant
  or allocating libc symbol.
- <a id="s5-3-p10"></a>[5.3¶10] **TS-2**, dynamic under ThreadSanitizer: eight threads share one compiled
  matcher and search different subjects concurrently across five
  differently-shaped engines; every threaded result must equal a
  single-threaded baseline. A planted race in a scratch copy of the driver
  must be caught, or the check fails itself.
- <a id="s5-3-p11"></a>[5.3¶11] **TS-3**, the library side: eight threads each compile their own pattern
  through `pcrec_compile()` concurrently, byte-matching a single-threaded
  baseline, TSan-instrumented and sabotage-validated. `pcrec_compile()` is
  safe to call concurrently (§8).

<a id="s5-4"></a>
### 5.4 Named groups: the `groups[]` index

<a id="s5-4-p1"></a>[5.4¶1] `rx_info.groups` is the named-group index: an array of `rx_group_entry`
(`name`, `number`, `slot`, `ref`) the artifact emits as the per-prefix array
`<prefix>_group_names` (only the ENTRY type is a fixed ABI type).
`rx_info.nnames` and `rx_info.nentries` count it (§6).

- <a id="s5-4-p2"></a>[5.4¶2] **`groups` is `NULL` and `nnames` is `0`** for a pattern that declares no
  named group, and also whenever module `named-groups` is not enabled for the
  compile — two different reasons. Under the bare default the module is off
  and `'(?<g>a)'` is refused with `requires module 'named-groups'`; with
  `--features named-groups` it compiles with `nnames = 1`.
- <a id="s5-4-p3"></a>[5.4¶3] **`slot`** is the group's caps index when the build delivers one, and `-1`
  otherwise. A named group forces the VM on a captures-on build, so a
  delivering row is never on a DFA artifact. Measured on `'a(?<b>b|c)+d'`
  with `--features named-groups`: captures-on emits `{ "b", 1, 1, NULL }`;
  `--no-captures` emits `{ "b", 1, -1, NULL }` and selects the DFA
  (`.engine = 1`). The captures-on artifact's `rx_info` reads
  `.ngroups = 1`, `.nnames = 1`, `.nentries = 1`, `.groups = rx_group_names`.
- <a id="s5-4-p4"></a>[5.4¶4] **The array is sorted by `(name ascending, number ascending)`**, name by
  `strcmp`: byte-exact and case-sensitive. `(?<name>a)(?<NAME>b)` is two
  distinct groups under libpcre2 10.46 and python `re` alike, under
  `(?i)`/`PCRE2_CASELESS` too — caseless folds matching, never name identity.
  This is libpcre2's own `PCRE2_INFO_NAMETABLE` order (measured:
  `tests/probes/probe_named_groups.c` declares `zeta`/`alpha`/`mu` and reads
  them back as `alpha`/`mu`/`zeta`; D59). On a composed artifact a leading
  SCOPE term precedes the key (§5.5).
- <a id="s5-4-p5"></a>[5.4¶5] **Duplicate names** (module `backrefs`' `(?J)`) form a RUN of rows ordered
  by ascending group number. The tiebreak is a correctness requirement (the emitted comparator is
  `src/gen/emit_dfa.c`'s `ng_cmp_name`, keyed `(scope, name, number)`):
  `tests/codegen/run_codegen_tests.sh`'s `[M6.5-DUPNAMES]` check asserts the
  rows strictly increasing in `(name, number)`, and sabotage S120 removes the
  tiebreak.

<a id="s5-4-p6"></a>[5.4¶6] **The caller's algorithm for a name that may be duplicated.** `bsearch`
`groups[0 .. nnames)` by name, which returns SOME row of the run; walk back to
the run's first row, then forward to the first row whose slot PARTICIPATED in
the match (both offsets set, set-to-empty included). That row is the group a
by-name reference resolves to — PCRE2's documented "first of the set that is
set" rule (measured; `docs/design/backrefs_design.md` §8.3) — and it is the
same algorithm the emitted `\k<name>` resolution uses, so caller and matcher
cannot disagree. A run none of whose members participated is an unset name.

<a id="s5-5"></a>
### 5.5 Composition: a library's delivered groups

<a id="s5-5-p1"></a>[5.5¶1] `pcrec` compiling a `.rxt` source composes: the target pattern's `(?&…)` calls
bind DEFINITIONS declared in that file or in a file it `lib`s
(`rxt_format.md` §1.2). A single-pattern artifact is unaffected by
everything in this section.

<a id="s5-5-p2"></a>[5.5¶2] **A library's groups are private unless both sides ask.** The DEFINITION lists
what it offers with an `export` line (default: nothing), and the CALL SITE
asks with a DELIVERING call. An exported name no site delivers costs no slot;
a delivering call on a definition that exports nothing is refused.

| in the pattern | what the caller gets |
|---|---|
| `(?&name)` | nothing: capture-transparent, as PCRE2 defines it |
| `(?&site=name)` | one row per exported group, named `site.group`, `ref` = the definition's name |
| `(?&=name)` | the same, with the definition's own name as the site |
| `(?&*=name)` | one row per exported group, named as exported, in the CALLER's own scope |

- <a id="s5-5-p3"></a>[5.5¶3] **A site is a scope.** Two delivering calls of one definition under two
  site names are two independent sets of rows and slots: `(?&a=email)…
  (?&b=email)` gives `a.local`, `a.host`, `b.local`, `b.host`, which do not
  alias.
- <a id="s5-5-p4"></a>[5.5¶4] **`(?&*=name)` puts rows in the caller's scope and keeps their provenance.**
  They are counted by `nnames` and found by §5.4's algorithm like the caller's
  own groups, so a clash with a caller's own group or another flat import is
  refused by name; and they still carry `ref`.
- <a id="s5-5-p5"></a>[5.5¶5] **A delivered group is addressed by NAME, never by number.** Its number
  depends on which definitions the target bound, in what order, and which
  sites delivered, so it may move when the library changes. Read
  `groups[i].name`, take `groups[i].slot`, never compute one.

<a id="s5-5-p6"></a>[5.5¶6] **What a delivered slot holds.** After a delivering call returns, the site's
slots hold what the callee matched on that call: spans are retained across
the return. This departs from PCRE2, whose plain subroutine call is
capture-transparent (`(?(DEFINE)(?<g>a))(?&g)` leaves group 1 unset); the `=`
opts into it. The definition's own copy of the group stays private and reads
`(-1,-1)`. For a non-recursive definition the oracle is exact: the
definition's body written out at the call site with its groups renamed
`site_x` is a legal PCRE2 pattern delivering the same spans. A delivering call
on a RECURSIVE definition is refused (delivery needs the callee inlined).

<a id="s5-5-p7"></a>[5.5¶7] **Which groups cost what:**

| the definition's group | a caps[] slot | a `groups[]` row |
|---|---|---|
| exported AND delivered by some site | one per delivering site | one per delivering site |
| referenced by the definition itself | one, private | no |
| neither | none — it spends no number | no |

- <a id="s5-5-p8"></a>[5.5¶8] **`ngroups` is the target pattern's own count**, and slots `1..ngroups` keep
  their permanent-prefix promise; everything a definition occupies is above
  it, so a composed artifact has `ngroups < ncaps - 1`.
- <a id="s5-5-p9"></a>[5.5¶9] **`nnames` counts the CALLER-SCOPE rows** (the pattern's own named groups
  plus flat imports), a genuine PREFIX of `groups[]`, which is sorted
  `(caller-scope first, name, number)`. §5.4's algorithm over
  `groups[0 .. nnames)` is correct unchanged and never walks into a
  site-scoped row.
- <a id="s5-5-p10"></a>[5.5¶10] **`nentries − nnames` is the number of SITE-SCOPED rows**,
  `[nnames .. nentries)`, each named `site.group`.
- <a id="s5-5-p11"></a>[5.5¶11] **The sort key is the SCOPE, not `ref`.** `ref` is non-NULL on every
  delivered row of either shape and says which definition a name came from;
  the scope says whether a caller may spell the name itself. A caller-scope
  name never contains `.`; a site-scoped one always does.
- <a id="s5-5-p12"></a>[5.5¶12] **`<PREFIX>_NCAPS` may move across library versions** while every index in
  `1..ngroups` holds still.

---

<a id="s6"></a>
## 6. `rx_info` — the reflection structure

<a id="s6-p1"></a>[6¶1] `<prefix>_info` is a `const struct rx_info` describing the artifact: what it
was built from, with which options, which engine and strategies it took, and
what working storage it needs. Its fields, in declaration order (the emitted
struct's own comments are short glosses of these rows; this table is the
contract). "Mirror" names the stamp macro (§6.3) carrying the same fact at
compile time, where one exists.


| # | field | type | meaning | mirror |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `abi` | `unsigned` | the version of the artifact's emitted scaffolding ([below](#s6-p17)); `71` | — |
| 2 | `flags` | `uint64_t` | the `PCREC_*` option bits as compiled, with the answer-preserving testing/tuning denials masked out ([below](#s6-p16)) | — |
| 3 | `encoding` | `int` | `PCREC_ENC_*`: `0` byte, `1` utf8 (§9.1) | — |
| 4 | `ncaps` | `int` | this artifact's caps slot count, all-in; always `== <PREFIX>_NCAPS` | `<PREFIX>_NCAPS` |
| 5 | `ngroups` | `int` | capturing groups in the pattern's own TEXT — a lexical fact, independent of `--no-captures` and of engine; on a composed artifact the TARGET pattern's own count ([counts](#s6-p3)) | — |
| 6 | `nnames` | `int` | caller-scope rows of `groups[]` — a prefix of the array (§5.4, §5.5) | — |
| 7 | `engine` | `unsigned` | `PCREC_ENGINE_DFA` (1) or `PCREC_ENGINE_VM` (2) | `<PREFIX>_ENGINE` (as a string) |
| 8 | `step_budget` | `int64_t` | the step budget; `-1` = none (every DFA artifact) | `<PREFIX>_STEP_BUDGET` |
| 9 | `work_budget` | `int64_t` | the work budget — the third bound (D47 second addendum): per-iteration forward work the fail label never sees, in work units, counted separately from steps; `-1` = none | `<PREFIX>_WORK_BUDGET` |
| 10 | `frame_capacity` | `int64_t` | the resume-frame capacity; `-1` = no bound (every DFA artifact) ([sentinel](#s6-p15)) | `<PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAMES` in the bounded case (a DFA artifact stamps `0` there) |
| 11 | `subject_ceiling` | `int64_t` | `0` = unset / not applicable; otherwise the stamped honest subject ceiling for a residually-unbounded capture body | — |
| 12 | `resume_frames` | `int64_t` | the stamped DEFAULT resume capacity, in frames; `0` = no resume stack (every DFA artifact) | `<PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAMES` |
| 13 | `trail_frames` | `int64_t` | the stamped default trail capacity, in entries; `0` on a DFA artifact | `<PREFIX>_TRAIL_FRAMES` |
| 14 | `resume_frame_size` | `int32_t` | bytes per resume frame, THIS artifact; `0` on a DFA artifact | `<PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAME_SIZE` |
| 15 | `trail_frame_size` | `int32_t` | bytes per trail entry; `0` on a DFA artifact | `<PREFIX>_TRAIL_FRAME_SIZE` |
| 16 | `pattern` | `const char *` | the source pattern text, as given to `pcrec_compile()`, embedded as an escaped C string literal | — |
| 17 | `pattern_len` | `size_t` | the byte count `pcrec_compile()` saw and compiled (§7) | — |
| 18 | `groups` | `const rx_group_entry *` | the named-group index, sorted; `NULL` when there is none (§5.4) | — |
| 19 | `engine_why` | `const char *` | prose: the construct or build outcome that forced the VM, or `NULL`; on a hybrid-eligible artifact it can also carry a prefilter note | `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_WHY` |
| 20 | `scan` | `const char *` | the DFA scan the artifact CONTAINS: `"unanchored"` / `"rev-end"` / `"attempt"` / `"empty"`; `NULL` when it contains none | `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN` |
| 21 | `prefilter` | `const char *` | the artifact's candidate-start mechanism; never `NULL` ([scan and prefilter](#s6-p6)) | `<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER` / `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER` |
| 22 | `match_form` | `const char *` | how `<prefix>_match` answers: `"unwrapped"` / `"search-filter"` / `"nomatch"`; `NULL` on every artifact whose `_match` the DFA emitter did not write — every VM artifact, hybrids included | `<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH` |
| 23 | `name` | `const char *` | the artifact's own name; never `NULL` ([name](#s6-p12)) | — |
| 24 | `nentries` | `int` | rows in `groups[]`, all of them (§5.4, §5.5) | — |
| 25 | `search_form` | `const char *` | how `<prefix>_search` recovers the match start: `"pinned"` / `"reverse-pass"` / `"attempt-start"`; non-`NULL` on every artifact that contains a DFA scan, a hybrid included; `NULL` only on a plain VM artifact | `<PREFIX>_DFA_START` |
| 26 | `vars` | `const char *const *` | the variable NAMES the pattern mentions, in first-mention order; `NULL` when none (`docs/spec/vars.md`) | — |
| 27 | `nvars` | `int` | entries in `vars[]` | `<PREFIX>_NVARS` (var-bearing artifacts) |
| 28 | `findings` | `const char *` | which findings each query the compile asked was answered from; `""` when none was asked; never `NULL` | `<PREFIX>_FINDINGS` (byte-identical) |

<a id="s6-p2"></a>[6¶2] Every field listed without a mirror is reachable only by reading
`<prefix>_info` at run time — `ngroups` included.

<a id="s6-p3"></a>[6¶3] **`ncaps`, `ngroups`, `nnames` and `nentries` are four different counts.**
`ngroups` is a fact about the pattern's text; `ncaps` about what THIS build
delivers (pinned to `1` on any DFA or `--no-captures` build however many
groups the text has); `nnames` and `nentries` about the named-group index.
`'a(b|c)+d'` compiled `--no-captures` has `ngroups = 1, ncaps = 1` — the
pattern has a group and the artifact delivers no slot for it, which a reader
of `ncaps` alone would miss; captures-on, `ngroups = 1, ncaps = 2`. The two
coincide (`ncaps - 1 == ngroups`) on a VM, captures-on, single-pattern
artifact.

- <a id="s6-p4"></a>[6¶4] **`ngroups` is a PERMANENT PREFIX-LENGTH promise** (D61). On any captures-on
  build, slots `1..ngroups` are this pattern's own groups in its own
  left-to-right numbering, so `ngroups <= ncaps - 1`, with equality on every
  build from a single pattern. Slots above `ngroups` belong to insertion and
  composition mechanisms, which APPEND and never interleave with or renumber
  the prefix (a composed artifact's bound definitions, §5.5). A caller
  indexing `caps` by the pattern's own group numbers is safe against every
  insertion feature. The promise pins the caps LAYOUT; `rx_group_entry.slot`
  remains the number-to-slot indirection for any other numbering.
- <a id="s6-p5"></a>[6¶5] **`nentries` equals `nnames` on every artifact built from a single
  pattern** and exceeds it on a composed one (§5.5). A caller that wants only
  the pattern's own names reads `nnames`; one that wants every row reads
  `nentries`.

<a id="s6-p6"></a>[6¶6] **`scan` and `prefilter`** are the run-time mirrors of the selection facts
§6.3 stamps, for a consumer with no preprocessor (a `dlopen`ing host, an FFI or
`ctypes` binding, a tool walking several `<prefix>_info` symbols in one image).
The rule, asserted over the whole corpus on both engines by
`tests/codegen/run_dfa_stamps.sh`:

| artifact | `scan` | `prefilter` |
|---|---|---|
| DFA artifact | `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN`'s value | `<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER`'s value |
| VM hybrid | the same, describing the DFA scan the artifact inlines | the same, describing that scan's own filter |
| VM, not a hybrid | `NULL` — no DFA scan | `"none"` (`<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER`'s value there) |

- <a id="s6-p7"></a>[6¶7] **`prefilter` is never `NULL`**: every artifact answers "what candidate-start
  mechanism do you carry", including "none".
- <a id="s6-p8"></a>[6¶8] **`scan != NULL` on a VM artifact means "this is a hybrid"** — the run-time
  reading of `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "hybrid"`.
- <a id="s6-p9"></a>[6¶9] **`"hybrid"` never appears in `prefilter`**: a hybrid reports its inlined
  scan's actual mechanism. A consumer wanting the coarse answer tests
  `scan != NULL`.
- <a id="s6-p10"></a>[6¶10] **The field and its macro are written from the same emitter functions and
  from nowhere else**, so they cannot disagree unless the emitter is wrong
  about both; "field == macro" is asserted on every compiled artifact.
- <a id="s6-p11"></a>[6¶11] **`match_form`'s NULL rule is not `scan`'s**: a hybrid contains a DFA scan,
  so `scan` is non-NULL there, but its `<prefix>_match` is the VM's anchored
  body, which `match_form`'s values do not describe, so `match_form` is NULL.
  `search_form` follows `scan`'s rule, because a hybrid inlines the DFA
  emitter's search body as its prefilter and so has a search form.

<a id="s6-p12"></a>[6¶12] **`name` says what the artifact IS; `<prefix>` says what its symbols are
called.** A `.rxt` source declares `target <prefix> = <definition>`, and a
definition may carry its own `name`, so one definition built under three
configs is three artifacts, three prefixes and ONE name — what a consumer
walking several `<prefix>_info` symbols needs to say "these are the same
matcher, built differently". A compile that supplies no name
(`pcrec_options.name == NULL`) stamps its own `<prefix>`, so `name` is never
`NULL` and a caller needs no NULL branch. It is arbitrary text, not an
identifier: nothing derives a symbol from it (`.rxt`'s own `name` grammar is
that format's rule, not this field's).

<a id="s6-p13"></a>[6¶13] **`pattern`** is embedded unconditionally as an escaped C string literal: `"`,
`\` and control bytes are escaped, by a string-literal escaper distinct from
the one that writes `/* … */` comments.

<a id="s6-p14"></a>[6¶14] **`findings`** mirrors `<PREFIX>_FINDINGS` because `rx_info` is the canonical
machine-readable record (D43): the macro alone is invisible to a linked
binary. It names the analysis a byte-rate came from in plain text, so a
shipped binary discloses the name of the analysis it was built under
(`docs/spec/findings.md` §5 states the grammar and the digest).

<a id="s6-p15"></a>[6¶15] **`frame_capacity`'s sentinel differs from the same-named option's.** On the
INPUT side `pcrec_options.frame_capacity == 0` means "let the compiler size
it" and a positive value is a request; on the OUTPUT side
`rx_info.frame_capacity == -1` means "no bound at all", which every DFA
artifact stamps (with `step_budget = -1` and `work_budget = -1`). `0` is not
a legal output value and `-1` is not a legal input value. `resume_frames`
carries the same number for the bounded case and `0` where there is no resume
stack.

<a id="s6-p16"></a>[6¶16] **`flags` records the REQUEST; the stamp macros record what the emitter DID.**
`flags` is `pcrec_options.flags` exactly as compiled with the testing/tuning
denials that change no answer masked OUT, so two identically-behaving
artifacts do not differ in their reflection surface. The rule is general and
derived: every axis bit is masked except the named kept set
(`docs/spec/tuning.md` §2, "THE `rx_info.flags` RULE"), so a new axis is
masked on arrival. The rule keeps the engine-selecting denials and the
contract axes (the startpos guard, bits 25 and 40, and `-futf-check`, bit 39),
the contract bits masked only under `byte`, where they are inert. Option bits
that are not axes (`PCREC_CASELESS`, `PCREC_NO_CAPTURES`, `PCREC_UCP`, …) are
reflected as compiled (§8.2). `tuning.md` §2 is
the per-bit catalogue and `tuning.md` §4 maps every bit to its
`pcrec_options` field; a caller that round-trips its own flags through
`rx_info.flags` finds the masked bits missing, legitimately. The macros, by
contrast, move when a denial is exercised: on `'(x)(?:a|bc)+d'`,
`-fno-possessify` moves `RX_VM_STRATS` from `0x1u` (POSSESSIVE) to `0x2u`
(BACKTRACKING) while `rx_info.flags` is unchanged; the whole initializer is
identical between the two builds except `frame_capacity`, because denying
possessification costs a frame. To see what was asked for on a masked axis,
`flags` cannot be used; to see what happened, read the macro.

<a id="s6-p17"></a>[6¶17] **`abi` is the version of the emitted SCAFFOLDING as a whole** (D76) — every
declaration, comment and macro the artifact carries, not only
`struct rx_info`'s layout. It is `71` on every artifact pcrec emits today; it
is mirrored by the `PCREC_RX_ABI_H` guard value (§1) and by the provenance
line (below), and by no macro.

- <a id="s6-p18"></a>[6¶18] **What changes at a bump:** any change to the emitted scaffolding for
  identical inputs, whether or not a struct offset moves — a new stamp line, a
  moved table, a changed comment, an appended field. A bump is paired with a
  re-pin of the codegen identity gate (`tests/codegen/
  run_recursion_identity.sh`, comparison (B)) in the same change.
- <a id="s6-p19"></a>[6¶19] **What is fixed within one `abi`:** the emitted output is byte-exact,
  whole-file, comments included, for a given pattern, prefix and option set.
  `-fcomments` and `-fno-comments` are two option sets whose artifacts differ
  in comment text and nothing else: the object file, the comment-excluded size
  and every emitted `#define` are identical between them. A caller diffing two
  artifacts compiled at one `abi` with one option set and finding a difference
  has found a pcrec bug.
- <a id="s6-p20"></a>[6¶20] **What a bump does not carry, pre-v1:** no compatibility story and no
  announcement beyond the number itself (D40 regime 1; the bumped number
  discharges D37's announced-boundary requirement). There is no deprecation
  cycle, migration note or advance notice. Do not build version negotiation on
  `abi` until a v1 declaration says what a bump means.
- <a id="s6-p21"></a>[6¶21] **New `rx_info` members are APPENDED**, so no existing offset moves when one
