  is added; `abi` still moves.

<a id="s6-p22"></a>[6¶22] `docs/dev/history/abi_changelog.md` records what each bump changed.

<a id="s6-p23"></a>[6¶23] **What a default artifact carries by way of comments** (`tuning.md` §2.24).
Exactly two things, under every setting: (1) the provenance line,
`/* Generated by pcrec VERSION (abi N). Pattern: <pattern> */`, on the `.c`
and on the paired `.h`, where VERSION is `PCREC_VERSION` (`lib/pcrec.h`; it
versions the tool, independently of `abi`) and N is `rx_info.abi`; and (2) the
shared `PCREC_RX_ABI_H` block's doc-comments — `rx_ctx`'s field notes,
`rx_matchfn`'s return-space paragraph, the give-up and below-the-floor code
notes, `rx_renderfn`, `rx_group_entry` and every `rx_info` member's note.
Everything else the emitter can say — orientation, table and state legends,
per-label roles, entry-point paragraphs, the residual entries' doc-comments,
the feature-set comment line — is emitted only under `-fcomments`. The paired
`.h` of a default build therefore records the feature set in no form;
`PCREC_FEATURE_SET` / `PCREC_FEATURE_MODULES` (§6.3) carry it on the `.c`.

<a id="s6-1"></a>
### 6.1 `rx_info` is link-time data

<a id="s6-1-p1"></a>[6.1¶1] `<prefix>_info` is not part of `rx_ctx` or any callback parameter: a caller
reads it by symbol, at whatever point it wants the artifact's facts about
itself. It is not strictly `.rodata`: `struct rx_info` holds pointers, so the
object needs load-time relocation. Measured with `readelf` on a default
`gcc -O2` object of `'a(b|c)+d'`: `rx_info` is a 200-byte object in
`.data.rel.ro.local` (writable-then-read-only) carrying one `R_X86_64_64`
relocation per non-`NULL` pointer member (seven there); the strings it points
at are in `.rodata`. There is no run-time initializer and no constructor; the
cost is those relocations at load. An embedder targeting ROM or flash plans
for the relocated section.

<a id="s6-3"></a>
### 6.3 The compile-time mirror: stamp macros

<a id="s6-3-p1"></a>[6.3¶1] An artifact carries compile-time macros — stamps — for a caller that wants to
`#if` on a fact rather than read a field at run time: D46's "every strategy
selection point must be observable".

<a id="s6-3-1"></a>
#### 6.3.1 Scoping rules

- <a id="s6-3-1-p1"></a>[6.3.1¶1] **Where they live.** The contract constants of the shared block (§2) and
  `<PREFIX>_NCAPS`, the sizing macros of §10.4 and, on a var-bearing artifact,
  `<PREFIX>_NVARS` are in the `.h` (measured: 29 `#define`s in the `.h` of both
  a VM and a DFA build of `'a(b|c)+d'`, identical except `RX_NCAPS`'s value
  and the sizing values). Every other stamp is emitted into the `.c` only, so
  reading one needs a self-contained artifact (`header_name == NULL`) or code
  inside the generated `.c` itself. Whether the stamps should also be emitted
  into the header is an open design question.
- <a id="s6-3-1-p2"></a>[6.3.1¶2] **The mirror is partial.** §6's table names, field by field, which `rx_info`
  members have a stamp; most stamps have no `rx_info` field. A stamp gets a
  run-time mirror only when a named consumer reads the fact at run time (D77);
  the stamps marked "no mirror" below have none for that reason, and adding one
  would be a struct append moving no existing offset. `match_form` and
  `search_form` have mirrors because each is a caller-visible COST property of
  an entry the caller calls; `_DFA_TABLE` and `_DFA_SCAN_EDGE` are internal
  encoding choices and have none.
- <a id="s6-3-1-p3"></a>[6.3.1¶3] **Two families.** (a) SELECTION FACTS — which engine, which candidate-start
  mechanism, which entry or search form, which pre-check — are stamped whether
  or not the mechanism fired (D81: a fact stamped only when it is interesting
  is a hint), on every artifact the mechanism can occur on. (b) CAPACITY and
  ACTIVITY macros report what the VM did — per quantifier, per call site, per
  frame — and are VM-only; a DFA artifact has no such activity. Several stamps
  report what the emitted code turned out to CONTAIN, discovered while
  emitting rather than chosen by a mode a caller can force
  (`<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS`, `_VM_ALT_ISLANDS`, `_VM_CLS_FOLDS`,
  `_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS`, and `_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE` under AUTO, which picks the rung
  after the program is emitted; `--vm-entry-shape=N` can name one).
- <a id="s6-3-1-p4"></a>[6.3.1¶4] **A stamp's scope is the MECHANISM it names, not the artifact kind.** Four
  scopes occur: every artifact; every artifact that CONTAINS a DFA scan (every
  DFA artifact and every VM HYBRID — a VM artifact whose
  `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER` reads `"hybrid"` and which inlines the DFA emitter's
  scan as a `static <prefix>_prefilter`); every VM artifact, hybrids included,
  never a pure-DFA artifact; and the narrower scopes named per stamp. A VM
  artifact carries the DFA-scan stamps IF AND ONLY IF it is a hybrid
  (`tests/codegen/run_dfa_stamps.sh` asserts it in both directions, with the
  emitted `<prefix>_prefilter` body as the independent third term).
- <a id="s6-3-1-p5"></a>[6.3.1¶5] **A fact is never readable by a macro's ABSENCE.** Within its scope every
  stamp is always emitted, `0` and `"none"` spelled as readily as any other
  value. A stamp whose value can legitimately be `0` and also needs a
  "declined" answer is a STRING with a `"none"` member, not a number with a
  sentinel.
- <a id="s6-3-1-p5a"></a>[6.3.1¶5a] **A start-table stamp names a selection the artifact RUNS.** The stamps that report a search-start choice (`<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW`, `_REQ_WHY`, `_REQ_HANDOFF`, `_DFA_PREFILTER`, `_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS`, `_VM_START_SCAN`, `_DFA_START`) carry that choice where the artifact's search path makes it, and the choice's ABSENCE value where it does not: `"none"` for the end window, the handoff and the prefilters, `"attempt-start"` for `_DFA_START`. `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN` names the path; the others never describe a pass the artifact does not run.
- <a id="s6-3-1-p6"></a>[6.3.1¶6] **`#if` on a stamp compiles only within its scope.** `#if`ing on
  `RX_ENGINE` is safe on every artifact; `#if`ing on a (b) macro such as
  `RX_VM_RUNGS` or a budget macro does not compile against a DFA artifact.
  (Measured by listing every `#define` in a fresh build of each kind.)
- <a id="s6-3-1-p7"></a>[6.3.1¶7] **Scalar, count or mask.** A per-artifact verdict is a scalar; a count is a
  whole-artifact total; a MASK is used only where the decision is taken per
  quantifier and a scalar would misreport a mixed artifact (`RX_VM_RUNGS`,
  `RX_VM_STRATS`, `RX_VM_PRUNES`, `RX_VM_POSS_ARMS`).
- <a id="s6-3-1-p8"></a>[6.3.1¶8] **One derivation per fact.** Each stamp is written from the same predicate
  or value the emitted code branches on, so a stamp cannot disagree with the
  code it describes unless the derivation itself is wrong.
- <a id="s6-3-1-p9"></a>[6.3.1¶9] **Stamps report; they never change answers.** Unless a row says otherwise, a
  consumer may conclude something about the artifact's cost, size or shape,
  never about its answers.
- <a id="s6-3-1-p10"></a>[6.3.1¶10] **Other `.c` macros** (slot indices `<PREFIX>_SLOT_*` and `<PREFIX>_NSLOTS`,
  the `<PREFIX>_R_*` return aliases, helper macros such as `<PREFIX>_PUSH`,
  `<prefix>_VALID_LB`) are internal to the artifact and not part of this
  contract.

<a id="s6-3-2"></a>
#### 6.3.2 Inventory

<a id="s6-3-2-p1"></a>[6.3.2¶1] Scope: **all** = every artifact; **dfa-scan** = every artifact containing a
DFA scan (DFA artifacts and VM hybrids); **dfa** = DFA artifacts only;
**vm** = every VM artifact, hybrids included; **hybrid** = VM hybrids only.
"Mirror" names the `rx_info` field.

| macro | scope | kind | mirror | section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PCREC_FEATURE_SET`, `PCREC_FEATURE_MODULES` | all | string | — | [§6.3.11¶1](#s6-3-11-p1) |
| `<PREFIX>_ENGINE` | all | token | `engine` | [§6.3.3¶1](#s6-3-3-p1) |
| `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL` | all | token | — | [§6.3.3¶3](#s6-3-3-p3) |
| `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_WHY` | vm | prose | `engine_why` | [§6.3.3¶2](#s6-3-3-p2) |
| `<PREFIX>_TUNE` | all | token | — | [§6.3.11¶2](#s6-3-11-p2) |
| `<PREFIX>_ALTCLS_MERGES`, `_ALTCLS_FACTORED` | all | count | — | [§6.3.11¶3](#s6-3-11-p3) |
| `<PREFIX>_STARTPOS_GUARD` | all | token | — | [§6.3.6¶2](#s6-3-6-p2) |
| `<PREFIX>_UTF_CHECK` | all | token | — | [§6.3.6¶3](#s6-3-6-p3) |
| `<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW` | all | string | — | [§6.3.7¶2](#s6-3-7-p2) |
| `<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE` | all | string | — | [§6.3.7¶4](#s6-3-7-p4) |
| `<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN` | all | string | — | [§6.3.7¶6](#s6-3-7-p6) |
| `<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY` | all | token | — | [§6.3.7¶8](#s6-3-7-p8) |
| `<PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF` | all | string | — | [§6.3.7¶10](#s6-3-7-p10) |
| `<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN` | all | token | — | [§6.3.7¶12](#s6-3-7-p12) |
| `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN` | dfa-scan | token | `scan` | [§6.3.4¶2](#s6-3-4-p2) |
| `<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER` | dfa-scan | token | `prefilter` | [§6.3.4¶3](#s6-3-4-p3) |

<a id="s6-3-3"></a>
#### 6.3.3 Engine selection

```c
#define RX_ENGINE        "vm"
#define RX_ENGINE_SEL    "selected"
#define RX_ENGINE_WHY    "capture group at pattern offset 1"
```

<a id="s6-3-3-p1"></a>[6.3.3¶1] **`<PREFIX>_ENGINE`** — which engine the artifact is; family (a), on every
artifact, both kinds written by one emitter function so the spellings cannot
drift. Mirrors `rx_info.engine`.

<!-- value-set: RX_ENGINE -->
| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `"dfa"` | a DFA artifact (`rx_info.engine == PCREC_ENGINE_DFA`) |
| `"vm"` | a VM artifact, hybrids included (`PCREC_ENGINE_VM`) |

<a id="s6-3-3-p2"></a>[6.3.3¶2] **`<PREFIX>_ENGINE_WHY`** — prose naming the construct or outcome that forced
the VM (`"capture group at pattern offset 1"`, `"--engine=vm"`), mirrored by
`rx_info.engine_why`. VM artifacts only: a DFA artifact was not forced, and its
`rx_info.engine_why` is `NULL` for the same reason. The first forcing reason
wins. It can also name a BUILD OUTCOME: under `--engine=auto` a DFA build that
overflows a cap (state count, table entries, the K7 element budget,
`tuning.md` §2.11) is a selection outcome, not a refusal, and the fallback
artifact stamps e.g. `"dfa overflowed: >32000 states at pattern offset 0"`;
the offset is 0 by convention, because the reason belongs to the whole
compile. Such an artifact can carry `RX_VM_PREFILTER "hybrid"` — the fallback's
first rung rebuilds the prefilter from the count-collapsed language, and
`RX_VM_PREFILTER_LANG_WHY "dfa overflow retry, exact nfa N"` says so
(`tuning.md` §2.5, §2.17) — or `"none"`. Where a real construct (a capture
request, a `VM_ONLY` registry row) also forces the VM, that reason wins the
stamp, and the overflow's effect on the prefilter still applies through a fact
this stamp does not carry. An emitted-SIZE refusal does not change it.

<a id="s6-3-3-p3"></a>[6.3.3¶3] **`<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL`** — the same decision as a CLOSED TOKEN a consumer
can bucket on; family (a), on every artifact, both engines. `_ENGINE_SEL` and
`_ENGINE_WHY` are written from one derivation at `src/opt/select_engine.c`'s
fit site; neither is parsed to produce the other. No `rx_info` mirror;
`rx_info.engine_why` mirrors the prose.

<!-- value-set: RX_ENGINE_SEL -->
| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `"selected"` | `auto` chose on the AST and nothing overflowed — the common case on both engines |
| `"forced"` | the caller named `--engine=vm` or `--engine=dfa`, so `auto` selected nothing |
| `"declined-nullable-default"` | `auto`, nothing overflowed, and the ordinary hybrid's own exact prefilter language admits the empty match on every path that matters (`empty_admits`), so its forward+reverse pair could never dismiss a position; no prefilter survives. A pattern whose every empty match crosses a non-multiline start AND end anchor (`^(\s+)*$`) is not declined, and a `${…}` pattern is never declined here (its variable turns the prefilter off first); both read `"selected"`. `-fprefilter` overrides the decline, and an explicit `--engine=vm` reads `"forced"` (`tuning.md` §2.17) |
| `"overflowed-dfa"` | `auto`, the DFA was to be the engine, its build overflowed a cap, and no prefilter survived the fallback |
| `"overflowed-prefilter"` | `auto`, the VM was already chosen for another reason, and only its auto-selected prefilter's DFA overflowed, so the prefilter was dropped |
| `"collapsed-prefilter"` | `auto`, a DFA build overflowed a STATE cap, and the retry kept a prefilter by rebuilding it from the count-collapsed language (`tuning.md` §2.5, §2.17) |
| `"declined-nullable"` | `auto`, a retry offered the count-collapsed prefilter and it was declined because the collapsed language is nullable; no prefilter survives, and the artifact is the one this compile produced without that retry (`tuning.md` §2.17) |
| `"size-cap-retry"` | an emitted-SIZE cap (not a DFA state cap) refused the exact artifact and a retry rebuilt a smaller one that shipped (`limits.md` §8). The artifact's own stamps say which rung: on a VM hybrid, the count-collapsed prefilter survived (`RX_VM_PREFILTER_LANG "count-collapsed"`) or the ladder's last rung DROPPED the prefilter (`RX_VM_PREFILTER "none"` with `RX_VM_PREFILTER_WHY`); on a DFA artifact, the anchored match-here machine was dropped (`RX_DFA_MATCH "search-filter"`) or the premultiplied table was (`RX_DFA_TABLE` off `"premultiplied"`) |

- <a id="s6-3-3-p4"></a>[6.3.3¶4] **The last five are all "fell back"**, which `_ENGINE_WHY` cannot express:
  the four overflow values share one prose string (`"dfa overflowed: …"`) and
  differ in what survived; `"size-cap-retry"` differs in which CAP fell back.
  A consumer asking "did this compile fall back?" tests for all five.
  `"declined-nullable-default"` is not among them: nothing overflowed, and it
  sits beside `"selected"`/`"forced"`.
- <a id="s6-3-3-p5"></a>[6.3.3¶5] **`"declined-nullable"` and `"overflowed-dfa"` are different outcomes**
  though both carry `RX_VM_PREFILTER "none"`: the first is a rescue refused as
  useless, the second one that was unavailable.
- <a id="s6-3-3-p6"></a>[6.3.3¶6] **`"declined-nullable-default"` and `"declined-nullable"` are one policy on
  two populations**: the second says a ladder rung offered a rescue and it was
  refused; the first says there was never a rung.
- <a id="s6-3-3-p7"></a>[6.3.3¶7] **The two size-cap rungs cannot both fire on one compile** (the prefilter
  rungs need a VM hybrid, the drop rungs a DFA artifact); which contributor a
  retry dropped is read off the artifact's own stamps.
- <a id="s6-3-3-p8"></a>[6.3.3¶8] **Under `--engine=vm` or `--engine=dfa` the value is `"forced"` and says
  nothing about a retry**, which is not gated on `auto`: a drop rung changes an
  entry-point FORM inside the engine the caller demanded, which is compatible
  with the demand, and no flag lets a caller demand the dropped machine
  (`-fno-anchored-dfa` is deny-only). Measured: `--engine=dfa --features unicode-props -e utf8 --
  '\p{L}'` compiles and stamps `"forced"`, where `auto` stamps
  `"size-cap-retry"`. A consumer of a forced compile reads `<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH`
  for whether an anchored machine exists, without its cause.

<a id="s6-3-4"></a>
#### 6.3.4 The DFA scan

<a id="s6-3-4-p1"></a>[6.3.4¶1] The stamps in this group describe the DFA SCAN and are on every artifact that
contains one — DFA artifacts and VM hybrids — except `<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH`,
which describes an ENTRY and is on DFA artifacts only. On a DFA artifact
measured on `'(?:[a-z]+)@(?:[a-z]+)'`, and on the hybrid `'a(b|c)+d'`:

```c
#define RX_ENGINE        "dfa"
#define RX_DFA_SCAN      "unanchored"
#define RX_DFA_PREFILTER "byte-class"
#define RX_DFA_TABLE     "premultiplied"
```
```c
#define RX_ENGINE        "vm"            /* the artifact's own engine */
#define RX_VM_PREFILTER  "hybrid"        /* the VM runs a DFA ahead of its program */
#define RX_DFA_SCAN      "unanchored"    /* ...and this is that DFA */
#define RX_DFA_PREFILTER "memchr"        /* ...and this is its candidate-start filter */
#define RX_DFA_TABLE     "premultiplied" /* ...and this is its table's encoding */
```

<a id="s6-3-4-p2"></a>[6.3.4¶2] **`<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN`** — which DFA scan the artifact contains; both shapes
otherwise stamp `RX_ENGINE "dfa"`, so this is the only way to tell them
apart. Mirrored by `rx_info.scan`.

<!-- value-set: RX_DFA_SCAN -->
| value | mechanism |
|---|---|
| `"unanchored"` | the O(n) forward scan from `search_from` (D7), followed by a reverse pass that recovers the match start unless `RX_DFA_START` is `"pinned"` |
| `"rev-end"` | every match ends at the subject's end or just before a final newline (`tuning.md` §2.46): the artifact's reverse machine walks back from each possible end, and the smallest accepting position is the match start; no forward scan runs unless a tie between the two ends needs one forward run from that start |
| `"attempt"` | the per-start-position computed-goto loop a `^`/`\A`-bearing pattern takes |
| `"empty"` | the start analysis proves the pattern matches nothing (`\B\b`, `\b\B`, `\d\b\w`, `a\bb`, and their `^`-anchored spellings): the search body is one `return 0` with no table, loop or skip, on either engine |

<a id="s6-3-4-p3"></a>[6.3.4¶3] **`<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER`** — the candidate-start mechanism of the scan.
Mirrored by `rx_info.prefilter` on a DFA artifact and a hybrid. Its values
are the whole set:

<!-- value-set: RX_DFA_PREFILTER -->
| value | mechanism |
|---|---|
| `"none"` | no candidate-start filter: the start state accepts (`start_acc` — no skip is sound; the largest cause, e.g. `a*`, `.*`, `\bx*`), every position is a candidate, or the artifact provably matches nothing |
| `"memchr"` | one candidate byte value at offset 0; a `memchr()` replaces the steps |
| `"byte-class"` | several at offset 0; a 256-entry `<prefix>_can_begin_match` bitmap walk |
| `"memchr-bounded"` | the `memchr` form under a `$`/`\Z`/`\z` view or a word context: bounded at `n - 1` and without the early `return 0` |
| `"byte-class-bounded"` | the bitmap form under the same, bounded at `n - 1` |
| `"offset-set"` | a SET of (offset, byte-set) tests, one scanned for and the rest verified on each candidate (`<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS`) |
| `"offset-set-bounded"` | the offset-set form under a view or word context, bounded at `n - 1` |
| `"run-pinned"` | the necessary run (`<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN`) sits at a fixed offset from every match's start and the scan already runs on its scan member there, so the candidate test verifies the whole run as one compare — the offset-set block with the run as one term; the run pre-check is then not emitted (`<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY "dominated"`). Removed by `-fno-run-prefilter` or `-fno-offset-skip` |
| `"run-pinned-bounded"` | the run-pinned form under a view or word context, bounded at `n - 1` |
| `"first-memchr-bounded"` | on a SEEDED machine (a `\b`, a lookbehind, a `(?m)` context) whose plain skip would test the start state's escape set `E`, the skip tests the pattern's start set `T` (the `start_set` fact) where `T` is a proper subset of `E` — here one byte, a `memchr()`; bounded at `n - 1`; a skip that moved re-seeds the scan state from the byte before its landing (`tuning.md` §2.42). Removed by `-fno-start-set` |
| `"first-class-bounded"` | the same with several start-set bytes: a 256-entry `<prefix>_start_bytes` table walk, bounded at `n - 1`. There is no unbounded start-set form: a seeded machine always carries the D11 bound |

<a id="s6-3-4-p4"></a>[6.3.4¶4] The `-bounded` forms are a real difference in what the mechanism buys: under
a view, a skip may not pass a position whose accept has not been evaluated,
so every skip stops one byte short and the `memchr` arm loses its early-out.

<a id="s6-3-4-p5"></a>[6.3.4¶5] **`<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS`** — which offsets the filter tests, as a
comma-separated ascending list of byte offsets from the candidate's start,
`*` marking the one the scan searches for:

```c
#define RX_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS "0,8*,13"   /* the uuid shape */
#define RX_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS "none"      /* every other value of _PREFILTER */
```

<a id="s6-3-4-p6"></a>[6.3.4¶6] Non-`"none"` exactly when `_DFA_PREFILTER` is one of the two `offset-set` or
two `run-pinned` values. On a `run-pinned` value it lists every offset the test
covers, the run's own offsets individually (`/user|/users`: `"0*,1,2,3,4"`),
and its scan may be offset 0 (`0*`), which no other value's scan is. Offset 0
is always a member. It is a second stamp rather than a widening of
`_DFA_PREFILTER` because that stamp's value set is the emitter's closed set of
FORMS, while this one is a fact about the individual machine.

<a id="s6-3-4-p7"></a>[6.3.4¶7] **`<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE`** — the encoding of the scan's transition tables
(`docs/design/premultiplied_dfa_table.md`, `tuning.md` §2.13, §3). A
selection fact, read off the predicate the emitted loop branches on. No
`rx_info` mirror.

<!-- value-set: RX_DFA_TABLE -->
| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `"premultiplied"` | every numeric transition table holds `next_state * classes`, so the step is `state = table[state + class]` |
| `"indexed"` | every one holds `next_state`, and the step multiplies |
| `"mixed"` | the machines took different forms — the choice is per machine, on its own `states * classes` and seed table (a machine that can start dead for some context byte is indexed). The machines are the forward one, the reverse one unless the search is pinned, and the anchored one under `<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH "unwrapped"` |
| `"none"` | the scan has no numeric transition table by construction: `_DFA_SCAN "attempt"` (states are labels, a step is a computed `goto`) or `"empty"` |

<a id="s6-3-4-p8"></a>[6.3.4¶8] The value names the selection that was MADE. After the uniform fold below, an
artifact can carry that selection without carrying a table: the stamp does not
fall to `"none"`, because the representation still fixes the folded constant
(`65535` under `"premultiplied"`, `-1` under `"indexed"`).

<a id="s6-3-4-p9"></a>[6.3.4¶9] **`<PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS`** — an integer COUNT: how many of the
artifact's DFA tables had all cells equal and are therefore NOT emitted, their
accessor returning the constant (keeping its state and class parameters, so a
call site's `subject[pos++]` is still evaluated). Two tables per machine are
foldable, `<m>_next_state` and `<m>_is_accepting`, over the same machines
`_DFA_TABLE` and `_DFA_SCAN_EDGE` compose (so none of the three can name a
machine the artifact does not contain), and the value runs `0..6`; `0` on `"attempt"` and
`"empty"`. It is family (b) in nature — what the emitted machine turned out to
contain — and is owed because a fold is visible only as a table's ABSENCE.
`tests/codegen/run_dfa_uniform_fold.sh` reads it. The artifact is smaller and
its scan cheaper by that many indexed loads; the answers are identical.

```c
#define RX_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS 4
```

<a id="s6-3-4-p10"></a>[6.3.4¶10] **`<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE`** — how the scan tests the class of a SCAN EDGE: a
maximal run of states differing only in how many bytes of one fixed class
have been counted, replaced by a bounded cursor loop and deleted from the
transition table (`tuning.md` §2.18; `src/opt/scanedge.c`). An edge's test is
the class-form table's answer for its class at the artifact's `--tune`
position and the scan site (`src/gen/clskit.c`, D139 item 2), spelled by the
emitters a VM class read uses. The six values below are all this macro ever
reads:

```c
#define RX_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "range"    /* (unsigned)(b - 97) <= 25u */
#define RX_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "none"     /* no machine carries a collapsible run */
```

<!-- value-set: RX_DFA_SCAN_EDGE -->
| value | mechanism |
|---|---|
| `"none"` | no scan edge: no machine has a collapsible run; `_DFA_SCAN "attempt"` (no loop-carried table load to shorten); `_DFA_SCAN "empty"`; or a build under `-fno-scan-edge` |
| `"range"` | every edge tests a contiguous byte range inline against immediates — `b == c`, `b <= hi` from 0, otherwise `(unsigned)(b - lo) <= span u` — so the loop touches no memory but the subject |
| `"fold"` | at `--tune=-2`/`-1` only: every edge's class is an ASCII case pair, tested `(b \| 0x20) == x`. At `0`/`+1`/`+2` a scan edge's fold pair is a `"bitmap"` (D138 Q1). Never under `-fno-cls-fold` |
| `"bitmap"` | at least one edge's class reads a 256-byte membership table; the loop-carried register is still the cursor |
| `"kit"` | at `--tune=-2`/`-1` only: every edge's class takes a `static inline` kit matcher `<prefix>_<machine>_scankit<N>`, smaller than its 256-byte table (`tuning.md` §2.33). Never at `0`/`+1`/`+2`, never under `-fno-cls-kit` |
| `"mixed"` | the artifact's edges took more than one form; the choice is per edge, and a machine may carry up to four |

<a id="s6-3-4-p11"></a>[6.3.4¶11] **`<PREFIX>_DFA_START`** — which of two forms the search entry takes to
recover the match START (§3.1); mirrored by `rx_info.search_form`. Its scope is
the DFA-scan scope, not `_DFA_MATCH`'s.

```c
#define RX_DFA_START "pinned"         /* the start is search_from, by compile-time proof */
#define RX_DFA_START "reverse-pass"   /* a second, backwards scan finds it */
#define RX_DFA_START "attempt-start"  /* no start recovery: an attempt began there */
```

<!-- value-set: RX_DFA_START -->
| value | mechanism |
|---|---|
| `"pinned"` | the forward machine's start state accepts unconditionally — at every position, under every view, in every class context — so every accept the forward loop records belongs to a thread that began at `search_from`, and the post-loop block writes that offset. The artifact carries NO reverse machine: no transition, accept or byte-class table, no stay or scan-edge tables, no `<prefix>_reverse_*` accessors, no reverse loop |
| `"reverse-pass"` | the artifact walks its reverse machine backwards from the match end to the furthest-back accepting position. Every `"unanchored"` artifact whose start state does not accept, or accepts depending on the position or the upcoming byte, or seeds into a state that may be dead, and any such build under `-fno-start-pinned` |
| `"attempt-start"` | the search recovers no start: its scan is `"attempt"` (each attempt begins at a known position, and a match is reported from the attempt that found it) or `"empty"` (nothing matches). No reverse pass runs (§6.3.1¶5a) |

<a id="s6-3-4-p12"></a>[6.3.4¶12] The two are answer-identical (`docs/design/opt5_step2_twopass.md` is the
proof; `tuning.md` §2.19 the axis).

<a id="s6-3-4-p13"></a>[6.3.4¶13] **`<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH`** — which of §3.2's two forms the artifact's
`<prefix>_match` and `<prefix>_match_caps` take; mirrored by
`rx_info.match_form`. Defined on exactly the artifacts whose `RX_ENGINE` is
`"dfa"`: on a hybrid the match entry is the VM's own anchored body, which this
value set does not describe.

```c
#define RX_DFA_MATCH "unwrapped"       /* its own anchored machine, run from ctx->pos */
#define RX_DFA_MATCH "search-filter"   /* the unanchored search, non-ctx->pos starts rejected */
#define RX_DFA_MATCH "nomatch"         /* the pattern matches nothing: -1 at once */
```

<!-- value-set: RX_DFA_MATCH -->
| value | mechanism |
|---|---|
| `"unwrapped"` | the artifact carries a third machine — the forward tables without the start-anywhere self-loop — and runs it from `ctx->pos` |
| `"search-filter"` | the entry runs `<prefix>_search` and rejects a match not starting at `ctx->pos`; the populations of §3.2. Only the size-cap drop among them reads `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "size-cap-retry"`; the others read their ordinary selection |
| `"nomatch"` | the artifact's scan is `"empty"`: the entry answers `-1` after the startpos check, with no scan (§3.2¶6a) |

<a id="s6-3-5"></a>
#### 6.3.5 The VM prefilter

```c
#define RX_VM_PREFILTER          "hybrid"
#define RX_VM_PREFILTER_LANG     "exact"
#define RX_VM_PREFILTER_LANG_WHY "no counted repeat"
#define RX_VM_RESEED             "exact"
```

<a id="s6-3-5-p1"></a>[6.3.5¶1] Three independent questions: whether the VM runs a DFA ahead of its program
(`_VM_PREFILTER`), what candidate-start filter that DFA's own scan carries
(`_DFA_PREFILTER`, §6.3.4), and which LANGUAGE the DFA recognises
(`_VM_PREFILTER_LANG`).

<a id="s6-3-5-p2"></a>[6.3.5¶2] **`<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER`** — on every VM artifact. `rx_info` has no field for
it; `rx_info.scan != NULL` is its run-time reading.

<!-- value-set: RX_VM_PREFILTER -->
| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `"hybrid"` | the VM runs a capture-erased DFA scan ahead of its program, inlined as `<prefix>_prefilter`; the artifact carries the §6.3.4 stamps |
| `"none"` | no DFA scan runs ahead; every attempt position is the VM's own |

<a id="s6-3-5-p3"></a>[6.3.5¶3] **`<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_WHY`** — emitted ONLY where the size-cap ladder's last
rung dropped the prefilter, and then beside `RX_VM_PREFILTER "none"` (the only
`"none"` it accompanies), reading `"size cap retry, hybrid N > CAP"`: the
refused exact artifact's bytes (not a discarded intermediate retry's) and the
cap it exceeded (`limits.md` §8; D135). The figure includes the
`<PREFIX>_MEMFN_*` stamp lines, which render before the size is measured.

<a id="s6-3-5-p4"></a>[6.3.5¶4] **`<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_LANG`** and **`_VM_PREFILTER_LANG_WHY`** — on exactly
the artifacts whose `_VM_PREFILTER` reads `"hybrid"`, and no DFA artifact
(`tests/codegen/run_dfa_stamps.sh` asserts it both ways). `_LANG_WHY` is prose
naming which of five reasons produced the value (`tuning.md` §2.17's table).
No `rx_info` mirror.

<!-- value-set: RX_VM_PREFILTER_LANG -->
| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `"exact"` | the count-collapse axis did not fire: the prefilter is not a count-collapsed superset |
| `"count-collapsed"` | the prefilter recognises a count-collapsed SUPERSET: every repeat with `rmin > 1` or `rmax > 1` lowered as `X{min(rmin,1),}`, so the machine does not scale with the count (`tuning.md` §2.17, K39) |

- <a id="s6-3-5-p5"></a>[6.3.5¶5] **The stamp reports the count-collapse axis ONLY** (D142). `"exact"` does
  not say the prefilter recognises the pattern's own language: a lookbehind, a
  lookahead, an atomic group or `\K` is erased from the prefilter's machine,
  which then over-approximates while this stamp reads `"exact"` (measured on
  76 lookbehind, 47 lookahead, 132 atomic and 53 `\K` hybrids,
  `docs/design/pf_know.md` §2.2/§8.4). Whether a successful prefilter also
  proves the match END is read from `<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED "exact"`.
- <a id="s6-3-5-p6"></a>[6.3.5¶6] **A prefilter is a filter either way**: its rejection is sound and its span
  start is a lower bound the VM verifies from, so the answers are identical
  (D46). A superset cannot bound the match END, so a `"count-collapsed"`
  artifact always reads `<PREFIX>_VM_PRUNE_CEILING "subject-end"`.

<a id="s6-3-5-p7"></a>[6.3.5¶7] **`<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED`** — what the hybrid's RETRY does after a failed attempt
(`tuning.md` §2.35, `docs/design/hyb_reseed.md`); same scope as
`_VM_PREFILTER_LANG`. The value is the name of the first-match row that fired
(`pcrec --list-axes`, axis `hyb-reseed`). No `rx_info` mirror.

<!-- value-set: RX_VM_RESEED -->
| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `"exact"` | the prefilter answers for the pattern's own language, so a failed attempt cannot follow one of its answers; the retry is the non-adaptive one |
| `"clamped"` | over-approximating prefilter on an artifact with an MRL clamp: the retry re-seeds after every failed attempt |
| `"anchored"` | over-approximating clamp-free prefilter on a start-anchored pattern (`_VM_START` not `"unanchored"`): the attempt loop stops after its first attempt, so no retry runs; the artifact equals its `-fno-hyb-reseed` artifact byte for byte |
| `"adaptive-dense"` | over-approximating clamp-free prefilter, and the compile's byte-rate prior predicts dense candidates: the retry steps or re-seeds per call, starting in step mode |
| `"adaptive"` | over-approximating clamp-free prefilter: the retry steps or re-seeds per call, starting with a short step budget |
| `"fixed"` | `-fno-hyb-reseed` on an over-approximating clamp-free prefilter: the non-adaptive retry |

<a id="s6-3-5-p8"></a>[6.3.5¶8] Every value answers identically, except that an `adaptive*` artifact runs a
subset of the attempts the non-adaptive retry runs and so can ANSWER where that
retry gave up on a budget — never the reverse (§3.1's skip rule; `tuning.md`
§2.35 says why clamped hybrids keep the non-adaptive retry).

<a id="s6-3-6"></a>
#### 6.3.6 The entries' character-position contract

<a id="s6-3-6-p1"></a>[6.3.6¶1] Both are family (a), on every artifact of both engines (the axis belongs to
the entries, not to an engine), read off the predicate the emitted entry text
is, and have no `rx_info` mirror; `rx_info.flags` carries the request bits,
masked where inert.

<a id="s6-3-6-p2"></a>[6.3.6¶2] **`<PREFIX>_STARTPOS_GUARD`** — what the entries do with a caller's
mid-character position (§9.2; `tuning.md` §2.23).

<!-- value-set: RX_STARTPOS_GUARD -->
| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `"guarded"` | a `startpos` (or `ctx->pos`) `> 0` inside a character is refused with `PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS` — the default under an encoding with multi-byte characters |
| `"align"` | `-fstartpos-guard=align`: such a position is moved forward to the next character start once, at entry; an anchored entry answers `-1` |
| `"permissive"` | the artifact answers at whatever position the caller named: `-fno-startpos-guard`, or an encoding (`byte`) where every position is a character start |

<a id="s6-3-6-p3"></a>[6.3.6¶3] **`<PREFIX>_UTF_CHECK`** — whether the entries refuse an ill-formed subject
(§9.4; `tuning.md` §2.36).

<!-- value-set: RX_UTF_CHECK -->
| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `"whole"` | `-futf-check`: every entry that takes a subject refuses with `PCREC_ERR_UTF` when an ill-formed sequence begins in `[startpos − LB, n)` |
| `"off"` | the default: invalid-tolerant; an ill-formed sequence matches nothing and is not reported |
| `"inert"` | the encoding has no ill-formed byte strings (`byte`); no check exists whatever was asked, and the artifact is byte-identical to one built without the flag |

<a id="s6-3-7"></a>
#### 6.3.7 Windows, necessary literals and start positions

<a id="s6-3-7-p1"></a>[6.3.7¶1] All six are family (a), on every artifact of both engines (a stamp varies by
engine family, never by presence within one; "does not apply" is a value),
and none has an `rx_info` mirror. None changes an answer, except where a row
says a give-up may become the answer.

<a id="s6-3-7-p2"></a>[6.3.7¶2] **`<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW`** — how far from the subject's end a match may begin.

```c
#define RX_END_WINDOW "4"      /* a match begins in [n - 4, n] */
#define RX_END_WINDOW "none"   /* nothing was proved */
```

<a id="s6-3-7-p3"></a>[6.3.7¶3] A string with a `"none"` member: `0` is a legal window (a `\z` pattern of
maximum width 0 may begin only at the end). The value is the bound both
search entries clamp to, from the same compile-time field as the clamp.
`"none"` is reported by a pattern that is not end-anchored, one of unbounded
width, one containing `\G`, one under a multi-byte encoding, and any build
under `-fno-end-window` (`tuning.md` §2.26). A non-`"none"` artifact does
constant work on an arbitrarily long subject; `"none"` does not mean "not
end-anchored".

<a id="s6-3-7-p4"></a>[6.3.7¶4] **`<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE`** — a byte every match must contain.

```c
#define RX_REQ_BYTE "62"       /* every match contains '>' */
#define RX_REQ_BYTE "none"     /* no byte is necessary on every path */
```

<a id="s6-3-7-p5"></a>[6.3.7¶5] A string with a `"none"` member (`0` is a legal byte). The value is the member
of the necessary set a subject is least likely to contain, by the resolved
analysis's `byte-rate` answer, with the rightmost rule as tiebreak and as the
whole answer where the answer is NONE (`tuning.md` §2.27;
`docs/spec/findings.md` §4 for which analysis answers). Where the necessary
RUN's scan member is an exact byte it is that member; where the run's scan
member is a two-member cube (`tuning.md` §2.39) it is the set's pick, or
`"none"` for an empty set; every value is a member of the necessary set. A
non-`"none"` artifact rejects a whole subject in one pass when the byte is
absent PROVIDED `<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY` reads `"emitted"`. `"none"` does not mean
"no required literal": a caselessly folded literal, an alternation with no
common byte and `-fno-req-byte` all report it.

<a id="s6-3-7-p6"></a>[6.3.7¶6] **`<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN`** — a literal run every match must contain.

```c
#define RX_REQ_RUN "2e746172@0"   /* every match contains ".tar"; the
                                     memchr scans member 0, '.' */
#define RX_REQ_RUN "53454c454354@4/dfdfdfdfdfdf"
                                  /* (?i)select: every match contains a
                                     member of each position (x & K) == T;
                                     the scan is the pair at position 4 */
#define RX_REQ_RUN "none"         /* no run of two or more bytes */
```

<a id="s6-3-7-p7"></a>[6.3.7¶7] The run's bytes as lowercase hex (a run is arbitrary bytes inside a
`#define`'s string body), `@`, and the index within them of the member the
emitted `memchr` scans for; `"none"` at a length below 2
(`<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE`'s case). `<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE` is exactly `bytes[idx]`
wherever position `idx` is an exact byte, which makes the two checkable
against each other. A run whose positions are not all exact bytes carries `/`
and each position's mask `K` in hex: `T` (the bytes) is each position's lower
member and `(x & K) == T` its membership test. `tuning.md` §2.28 carries the
derivation.

<a id="s6-3-7-p8"></a>[6.3.7¶8] **`<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY`** — whether the artifact acted on either fact, and why
not; a closed token set (`tuning.md` §2.29).

```c
#define RX_REQ_WHY "emitted"      /* or "none", "one-attempt", "dominated" */
```

<!-- value-set: RX_REQ_WHY -->
| value | what it says |
|---|---|
| `"emitted"` | the artifact emits a pre-check on the byte or run its siblings name — possibly led by a rarer necessary-set byte's one-byte check (`tuning.md` §2.40), possibly handing off (`<PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF`) |
| `"none"` | nothing is necessary: no byte and no run (none found, or `-fno-req-byte`) |
| `"one-attempt"` | declined: the search route tries ONE start position, so a whole-window pass in front of it only adds work |
| `"dominated"` | declined: the artifact's own candidate-start `memchr` (or run-pinned test) already scans a byte at least as rare, or its locator decides presence itself (`<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN "rev-end"` or `"empty"`) |

<a id="s6-3-7-p9"></a>[6.3.7¶9] `"none"` holds if and only if `<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE` and `<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN` are
both `"none"`. Any other value asserts that a byte or run was derived, and only
`"emitted"` asserts that the artifact tests it: a consumer asking "does this
artifact reject a subject in one pass" reads this stamp, then its siblings for
the value.

<a id="s6-3-7-p10"></a>[6.3.7¶10] **`<PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF`** — where the search body's scan begins.

```c
#define RX_REQ_HANDOFF "2"     /* the scan begins 2 bytes before the run
                                  pre-check's first window hit */
#define RX_REQ_HANDOFF "none"  /* the scan begins at startpos */
```

<a id="s6-3-7-p11"></a>[6.3.7¶11] A decimal `K` where the `req-use` table's `handoff` row applies
(`tuning.md` §2.41): an emitted run pre-check (`_REQ_WHY "emitted"` with a
`_REQ_RUN`), a DFA scan in front of the body (a DFA artifact, or a hybrid's
prefilter), a finite `K`, a prefilter that is not count-collapsed, and not a
hybrid with a `\G` start family whose prefilter window is its match ceiling.
Then every match begins at most `K` bytes before an occurrence of the run's
window; the pre-check's search block returns the LEAST position `>= startpos`
at which the whole window occurs (or `n` when none does — the position itself
is meaningful, not only its comparison with `n`); and the body begins its scan
at `max(startpos, that − K)`, rounded up to a character start under a
multibyte encoding when it moved. The three bodies with a DFA scan read it at
their one start site; `\G` keeps reading `startpos`. `"none"` everywhere else,
including any build under `-fno-req-handoff`. `K` is the `req_run_maxoff` fact
`--emit-facts` lists (`facts_listing.md` §4.1.2), in BYTES: `(?i)straße` under
`-e utf8` reads `"2"`, because `(?i)s` matches U+017F, two bytes, before the
window `TRA`. A non-`"none"` value never changes an answer or a give-up.

<a id="s6-3-7-p12"></a>[6.3.7¶12] **`<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN`** — where a VM attempt can start.

```c
#define RX_VM_START_SCAN "first-class"  /* attempts start only where the
                                           byte is in the start set */
#define RX_VM_START_SCAN "none"         /* every position is attempted */
```

<!-- value-set: RX_VM_START_SCAN -->
| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `"first-class"` | the candidate table's VM-route row applies (`tuning.md` §2.42): a VM artifact with `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "none"`, an unanchored pattern, and a start set (the `start_set` fact, `facts_listing.md`) that cannot match empty and has fewer than 256 members. The attempt loop seeks the next byte of that set through a 256-entry table — after the range guard, the boundary guard, `<prefix>_valid_upto` and the necessary-set pre-check — before its first attempt and after each failed one, and answers no-match where none is left |
| `"none"` | every DFA artifact, every hybrid (whose prefilter is its start test), every anchored or `\G`-start pattern, and any build under `-fno-start-set` |

<a id="s6-3-7-p13"></a>[6.3.7¶13] The value names the FORM of the seek; a one-byte (`memchr`) form is not built.
A non-`"none"` value never changes an answer; a give-up may become the answer
(§3.1).

<a id="s6-3-8"></a>
#### 6.3.8 VM capacity and activity

<a id="s6-3-8-p1"></a>[6.3.8¶1] All are on every VM artifact, hybrids included, and never on a pure-DFA
artifact, unless the row says otherwise. None has an `rx_info` mirror except
the budgets. A VM build of `'a(b|c)+d'`:

```c
#define RX_VM_RUNGS         0x1u
#define RX_VM_STRATS        0x1u
#define RX_VM_POSS_ARMS     0x0u
#define RX_VM_PRUNES        0x1u
#define RX_VM_PRUNE_CEILING "prefilter-window"
```

<a id="s6-3-8-p2"></a>[6.3.8¶2] **The four masks.** Each is the OR of what the artifact's quantifiers used,
built from the named bit constants of the shared block (§2):

- <a id="s6-3-8-p3"></a>[6.3.8¶3] `<PREFIX>_VM_RUNGS` — which per-quantifier rungs: `PCREC_VM_RUNG_CURSOR`,
  `_FRAMES_BOUNDED`, `_FRAMES_UNBOUNDED`, `_REVDET`, `_COUNTER`.
- <a id="s6-3-8-p4"></a>[6.3.8¶4] `<PREFIX>_VM_STRATS` — `PCREC_VM_STRAT_POSSESSIVE` / `_BACKTRACKING`.
- <a id="s6-3-8-p5"></a>[6.3.8¶5] `<PREFIX>_VM_PRUNES` — `PCREC_VM_PRUNE_CLAMPED` / `_UNCLAMPED` (MRL).
- <a id="s6-3-8-p6"></a>[6.3.8¶6] `<PREFIX>_VM_POSS_ARMS` — the per-ARM half of `_VM_STRATS`' POSSESSIVE bit:
  `0x1` (A0, a lookahead-born gate in the follow valued with nothing known on
  its left), `0x2` (A1, a gate valued by the loop's own last characters'
  polarity) and `0x4` (B, a backreference's first character read from its
  groups), each set when that arm was NEEDED for some positive possessify
  verdict — for A1, decided by A1 alone; for A0 and B, the same compile with
  that arm denied counts fewer positive verdicts. `0x0u` where no arm was
  needed, including every artifact built with both arms denied (a denied arm's
  bit is 0 by construction; `tuning.md` §2.44/§2.45). These bit values are
  this paragraph's; they are not named constants in the shared block.

<a id="s6-3-8-p7"></a>[6.3.8¶7] **`<PREFIX>_VM_PRUNE_CEILING`** — the match-end ceiling the length pruning
clamps against: `"prefilter-window"` (the hybrid prefilter's span end),
`"subject-end"`, or `"none"` (no length pruning, e.g. `-fno-length-prune`).
`--emit-ir`'s `prune-ceiling` row uses the same three words
(`ir_listing.md` §3.1.2).

<a id="s6-3-8-p8"></a>[6.3.8¶8] **`<PREFIX>_VM_CALL_SPLICED`** and **`<PREFIX>_VM_CALL_LINKED`** — on
call-bearing VM artifacts only: the number of subroutine-call sites spliced
inline and the number linked as calls (`tuning.md` §2.9). A spliced call adds
nothing to a resume frame; a linked one does (§10.2).

<a id="s6-3-8-p9"></a>[6.3.8¶9] **`<PREFIX>_VM_ROOT_MINW`** — emitted only on a VM artifact whose pattern's
minimum width is at the analysis ceiling (the language is EMPTY); its
`<prefix>_search` answers no-match before any frame is pushed.

<a id="s6-3-8-p10"></a>[6.3.8¶10] **`<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS`** — `1` if and only if the VM program emits no
`RX_PUSH` site and no linked call, i.e. the fail label has no pop-and-resume
`goto *` dispatch; `0` otherwise. A scalar boolean (a whole-artifact fact).
`1` also means the artifact's eight entry-chain statics are ELIGIBLE for
`static inline __attribute__((always_inline))`; `<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE` says
which carry it. `0` means none does (a framed artifact is `"plain"` by
construction: gcc refuses `always_inline` on a function containing a computed
goto).

```c
#define RX_VM_FRAMELESS 1   /* or 0 */
```

<a id="s6-3-8-p11"></a>[6.3.8¶11] **`<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE`** and **`<PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES`** — the rung
the emitter took for the artifact's six entries, and the program size it was
chosen from (`tuning.md` §2.21).

```c
#define RX_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE   "forward"   /* or "plain", "shared", "inline" */
#define RX_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES 646ULL
```

<!-- value-set: RX_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE -->
| value | shape |
|---|---|
| `"plain"` | one body, six framed entries; no entry-chain static carries `always_inline` |
| `"shared"` | one out-of-line body behind three forwarding entries; seven of the eight statics carry `always_inline`, the matcher is `noinline` |
| `"forward"` | three bodies in the three `_in` entries, three forwards; all eight statics carry `always_inline` |
| `"inline"` | six bodies; all eight statics carry `always_inline` |

<a id="s6-3-8-p12"></a>[6.3.8¶12] A closed token fixed at four by the emitter's own enum. `_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES` is
the emitted VM program size in bytes — the exact quantity
`VM_INLINE_CHAIN_MAX_BYTES` was compared against when AUTO chose the rung —
measured at the canonical two-byte prefix length: the program is emitted under
a two-byte placeholder prefix and the caller's `-p` spelling is written onto
the finished text, so the number and the rung are the same under every prefix
(`limits.md` "Size limits and the prefix"). The second macro is what makes the
first checkable: `"plain"` has four causes — framed, forward-illegal above the
size term, tiered, or asked for — which `_VM_FRAMELESS` and the size against
the stamped limit tell apart. Both are scalars.

<a id="s6-3-8-p13"></a>[6.3.8¶13] **`<PREFIX>_VM_ALT_ISLANDS`** — the number of flat alternations the VM lowered
as an ALTERNATION ISLAND, a trie dispatch over the alternation's literal
alternatives, rather than as a serial resume chain (`tuning.md` §2.20). A
count, because the island is chosen per alternation. Such an artifact
dispatches its alternations by byte, so its cost on a wide alternation does not
scale with the winner's branch index and its size does not depend on the order
the alternatives were written; the island reports the same alternative, in the
same backtracking order, as the chain. A DFA route has no such decision.

```c
#define RX_VM_ALT_ISLANDS 1   /* or 0, or more */
```

<a id="s6-3-8-p14"></a>[6.3.8¶14] **`<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_FOLDS`** — the number of the VM program's class-pool
entries tested in the ASCII-FOLD shape: a two-member set differing only in
bit `0x20`, both letters, tested `(byte | 0x20) == lower` with no 32-byte
bitmap emitted for it (`tuning.md` §2.22), chosen by the fold rows of
`src/gen/clskit.c`'s class-form table. Distinct fold classes carry distinct
compare constants, so a structural check can hold the count to the text. A DFA
scan edge's fold is reported by `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "fold"`, not here.

```c
#define RX_VM_CLS_FOLDS 6   /* or 0, or any count */
```

<a id="s6-3-8-p15"></a>[6.3.8¶15] **`<PREFIX>_VM_LIT_RUNS`** — the number of literal-run compares the VM program
writes: a run of three or more one-byte literals in a concatenation (a
two-byte run stays a two-node byte chain), and an alternation island's
single-child trie chain, each one bounds check and one run compare — a
constant-length `memcmp`, or at the lengths gcc decomposes two overlapping
word compares (`tuning.md` §2.31, §2.38). `0` under `-fno-lit-run`.

```c
#define RX_VM_LIT_RUNS 5   /* or 0, or any count */
```

<a id="s6-3-8-p16"></a>[6.3.8¶16] **`<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_KIT`** — the number of distinct class-matcher functions
the VM program calls: `<prefix>_wcls<N>` (a wide class, more than one member
and some member deeper than one code unit, tested as `<prefix>_decode` plus
one matcher) and `<prefix>_class_kit<N>` (a byte class tested by the kit's
form at `--tune=-2`/`-1` where the kit is smaller than the class's table;
`tuning.md` §2.33). `<prefix>_decode` is a `static inline` encoding-seam
helper declared nowhere. A DFA scan edge's kit matcher is not counted here.
`0` under `-fno-cls-kit`, and under `-e byte` at `0`/`+1`/`+2`. Which form a
matcher took is `--emit-ir`'s `consume` row and the matcher's own text.

```c
#define RX_VM_CLS_KIT 1   /* or 0, or any count */
```

<a id="s6-3-8-p17"></a>[6.3.8¶17] **`<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_ATOMS`** — non-zero exactly when the VM program tests its
table-read byte classes through ONE shared byte-to-atom table,
`static const unsigned char <prefix>_class_atoms[256]`, with one `static
inline` matcher `<prefix>_class_atom<N>` per class (one load, one shift of a
64-bit immediate); then it is the number of atoms the table numbers, `1..64`
(`tuning.md` §2.34). The table is taken where at least 11 table-read byte
classes exist and the byte partition has at most 64 atoms, and it is selected
after the entry rung. `0` means a 32-byte bitmap per class, or no table-read
class. `0` under `-fno-cls-pack`; `-fno-cls-kit` denies the atom table too.

```c
#define RX_VM_CLS_ATOMS 0   /* or the shared table's atom count, 1..64 */
```

<a id="s6-3-8-p18"></a>[6.3.8¶18] **`<PREFIX>_VM_START`** — where an attempt may begin; a closed token.

```c
#define RX_VM_START "anchored"   /* or "gstart", or "unanchored" */
```

<!-- value-set: RX_VM_START -->
| value | what it says |
|---|---|
| `"anchored"` | every alternative of the whole pattern begins with `^` (outside multiline) or `\A`, so only offset 0 can start a match |
| `"gstart"` | every alternative begins with `\G`, so only the caller's `search_from` can start a match |
| `"unanchored"` | nothing was proved, or `-fno-vm-anchor-bound` was given |

<a id="s6-3-8-p19"></a>[6.3.8¶19] Either non-`"unanchored"` value means the emitted search loop stops after one
attempt (`tuning.md` §2.25). The fact is `pcrec_start_anchor`'s, derived above
either engine; on a DFA artifact the same fact is legible through
`<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN "attempt"`. `"unanchored"` does not mean "not anchored": a
denied build and a backreference-leading pattern report it too.

<a id="s6-3-8-p20"></a>[6.3.8¶20] **`<PREFIX>_STEP_BUDGET`** and **`<PREFIX>_WORK_BUDGET`** — the budgets the
artifact was built with, mirrored by `rx_info.step_budget` / `work_budget`
(values: `limits.md` §3).

<a id="s6-3-8-p21"></a>[6.3.8¶21] **`<PREFIX>_FAST_FRAMES`** and **`<PREFIX>_FAST_TRAIL`** — the capacities the
un-suffixed entries' FAST TIER runs on (§10.9), on every VM artifact,
single-tier ones included.

```c
#define RX_FAST_FRAMES  47   /* tiered: below the stamped default */
#define RX_FAST_TRAIL   71
```

<a id="s6-3-8-p22"></a>[6.3.8¶22] `<PREFIX>_FAST_FRAMES == <PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAMES` is the statement "this
artifact has one tier", and the only spelling of it. Four things produce it:
the stamped default already fits a page, the slot array alone does not, the
scaled fast tier would be too small to be worth two runs, or
`-fno-tiered-entry`; they are not distinguishable from `rx_info.flags`, in
which `-fno-tiered-entry` is masked. They are `.c`-private: no entry takes a fast capacity and
no caller sizes anything from one, and a caller's code should not branch on
the tier boundary.

<a id="s6-3-9"></a>
#### 6.3.9 The size term and the size caps

<a id="s6-3-9-p1"></a>[6.3.9¶1] **`<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K`** and **`<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K_WHY`** — on every VM
artifact: the unroll factor the artifact was emitted at, and why
(`tuning.md` §2.10, §2.16; `limits.md` §8a). Selection facts stamped whether or
not the term fired (D81).

<!-- value-set: RX_UNROLL_K_WHY -->
| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `"option"` | an explicit `--unroll=K` |
| `"denied"` | `-fno-size-term` |
| `"default"` | the term ran and the artifact was below its threshold |
| `"size-model"` | the ladder ran and its `K` was taken |
| `"size-model-declined"` | the ladder ran and the materiality bar rejected its `K` |
| `"cap-rescue"` | the bar declined a `K` and an emitted-size cap took it anyway |
| `"capacity-declined"` | the ladder ran and the `K` it wanted would have LOWERED the artifact's declared capacity (`.frame_capacity` or `.subject_ceiling`) below what the default `K` declares, so it was not a candidate (`limits.md` §8a) |

<a id="s6-3-9-p2"></a>[6.3.9¶2] **`<PREFIX>_MAX_EMIT_CODE_BYTES`** (VM artifacts) and
**`<PREFIX>_MAX_EMIT_BYTES`** (every artifact; the total-bytes cap applies to
whatever was emitted) — the EFFECTIVE emitted-size limits the artifact was
built under, so an artifact that fitted can be told from one built with a
raised cap without the command line (`limits.md` §8).

<a id="s6-3-10"></a>
#### 6.3.10 Artifact-wide counts and the search-code kit

<a id="s6-3-10-p1"></a>[6.3.10¶1] These are on every artifact, both engines, written after the engine body,
beside the `rx_info` definition, in this order: `<PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS`,
`<PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS`, `<PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC`, `<PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES`,
then `<PREFIX>_FINDINGS`. The first three are written by pcrec-memory-functions
(`memfn/`, D146/D147).

<a id="s6-3-10-p2"></a>[6.3.10¶2] **`<PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS`** — the number of literal-run compares the artifact
writes as WORD compares, counting each compare once whatever engine wrote it:
the `overlap` row (an exact run of length 3, 5-7 or 9-15) and the `words` row
(a masked run; `tuning.md` §2.38, §2.39). Any other exact run compare is a
`memcmp` and is not counted. `0` where none is written and under
`-fno-run-overlap`. An unquoted integer. It is on both engines because the run
compare writes the DFA scan's run term and run pre-check as well as the VM's
literal runs and island chains (since the kit owns the run compare,
`memfn/src/runcmp.c`).

```c
#define RX_RUN_WORDS 1   /* or 0, or any count */
```

<a id="s6-3-10-p3"></a>[6.3.10¶3] **`<PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS`** and **`<PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC`** — what the search-code
kit rendered, and which C library functions the artifact calls.

```c
#define RX_MEMFN_FORMS "none"
#define RX_MEMFN_LIBC "memchr,memcmp"   /* or "none" */
```

- <a id="s6-3-10-p4"></a>[6.3.10¶4] **`MEMFN_FORMS`** is `"none"` iff the artifact is byte-identical (stamp
  lines aside) to its own `-fno-memfn-simd` compile; otherwise the ids of the
  forms that make it differ, comma-joined in site order, a site that cascades
  between ISA levels carrying them as `ID@LEVEL+LEVEL`. Ids and level names are
  OPAQUE: bucket on `"none"` / not-`"none"`, never parse an id. SIMD is off by
  default and no SIMD form exists, so the value is `"none"` on every artifact
  today (D147 addendum 10, Q55). A scalar-layer kit change does not change it;
  such a change is attributed by its `abi` event and its `--memfn=no-NAME`
  deny row, and a consumer that must tell two same-`abi` builds apart records
  the build recipe (`abi`, pcrec commit, argv).
- <a id="s6-3-10-p5"></a>[6.3.10¶5] **`MEMFN_LIBC`** is `"none"` or the names of the C library functions the
  artifact's code calls, sorted (byte order), distinct, comma-joined with no
  space: a SOURCE-LEVEL inventory of the whole artifact (search code, variable
  resolver, an `--emit-main` driver, `--trace` output; comments and string
  literals excluded), not a promise of a dispatched call — a name is listed
  even where the compiler later inlines or folds the call. A `memcpy` of a
  constant 1-8 bytes is a register load and is not listed (the literal-run
  word loads, `<prefix>_wN`); data objects (`stderr`) are not functions and
  are not listed. A SIMD-off artifact that lists `memchr` delegates that search
  to the C library's own dispatch.
- <a id="s6-3-10-p6"></a>[6.3.10¶6] Neither carries a kit version or vocabulary number, so a kit release that
  moves no emitted byte moves neither.
- <a id="s6-3-10-p7"></a>[6.3.10¶7] **Checked by C11** (`make test-memfn-stamps`,
  `tests/memfn/run_libc_census.sh`): over a corpus-wide sample every artifact
  carries both lines, and `MEMFN_LIBC` equals the undefined function symbols
  of the artifact's `-O0 -fno-builtin` object minus the constant-size `memcpy`
  loads. `MEMFN_FORMS`' identity half compares default against
  `-fno-memfn-simd` (`tuning.md` §2.43), reported "identical (no SIMD form)"
  while no SIMD form exists; its movers half stays unreached until one does.

<a id="s6-3-10-p8"></a>[6.3.10¶8] **`<PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES`** — how many bytes of the artifact sit under a
CPU-level guard; written by pcrec directly after `<PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC`, an
unsigned 64-bit integer spelled as 16 hex digits.

```c
#define RX_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES 0x0000000000000000ULL   /* or any count */
```

<a id="s6-3-10-p9"></a>[6.3.10¶9] It is the number of bytes the search-code kit wrote between its `simd_open`
and `simd_close` sink calls (the `#if <level>` blocks a SIMD-on form adds: its
per-level helpers and the guarded arms of its selector,
`docs/design/memfn/integration.md` §R4.9.2.4), counted in the unit every pcrec
length decision uses: comment bytes `-fno-comments` dropped are included, and
the symbol prefix is counted at a fixed width, so neither `-fno-comments` nor
`-p` changes the value. It is zero on every artifact that holds no such block,
which is every artifact today: no SIMD form exists and `-fmemfn-simd` is inert
(`tuning.md` §2.43). It is the artifact's size beyond its SIMD-off compile.
Those bytes are invisible to every pcrec size DECISION — the VM entry-shape
knee and `<PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES`, the size term and its ladder, and the D84
caps (`limits.md` §8) all read the length minus these bytes — so turning SIMD
on moves no rung, ladder step, refusal or other stamp's value. There is no
aggregate budget (D155 addendum 2): each SIMD row bounds its own guarded bytes.
**Checked by** `make test-memfn-guarded` (`tests/memfn/run_simd_guarded.sh`):
every artifact of a corpus sample carries the line, its value is at most the
sum of the declared bounds of the forms `<PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS` lists (0 while
that is `"none"`), and a test-only build writing a synthetic guarded block
through the same sink calls must equal the plain build, block and stamp value
aside.

<a id="s6-3-10-p10"></a>[6.3.10¶10] **`<PREFIX>_FINDINGS`** — which findings this artifact was built from;
mirrored byte for byte by `rx_info.findings`.

```c
#define RX_FINDINGS "byte-rate=default:1822fb973b95a4da"
#define RX_FINDINGS "byte-rate=none"   /* asked; nothing answered (-e utf8) */
#define RX_FINDINGS ""                 /* nothing asked */
```

<a id="s6-3-10-p11"></a>[6.3.10¶11] One `query=bundle:digest` item per findings query the compile ASKED, in the
fixed query order, `;`-joined; `query=none` where the analysis declares
nothing for this compile's encoding; the empty string when no reader asked
(`docs/spec/findings.md` §5: the grammar and the digest's byte layout).
`bundle` is the analysis whose block answered, and the digest covers exactly
what the readers consumed, so two artifacts built from the same rates carry
the same stamp. It is written after every reader has run, so an ask made while
the engine body is emitted is recorded. The bundle name is plain text in the
artifact.

<a id="s6-3-11"></a>
#### 6.3.11 Feature set, tuning position, alternation normalization

<a id="s6-3-11-p1"></a>[6.3.11¶1] **`PCREC_FEATURE_SET`** and **`PCREC_FEATURE_MODULES`** — the feature-module
set the artifact was built with (D37; §1): the named set, and the
comma-separated modules. Under `--features all` every module's name is listed,
whether or not the pattern uses it. `PCREC_*`-named but per-artifact, in the `.c`.

<a id="s6-3-11-p2"></a>[6.3.11¶2] **`<PREFIX>_TUNE`** — the `--tune` position, a closed five-token string
(`tuning.md` §5.3). At the default `"balanced"` nothing else differs from a
build with no `--tune` flag; at no position does an answer move
(`tuning.md` §5.5).

<a id="s6-3-11-p3"></a>[6.3.11¶3] **`<PREFIX>_ALTCLS_MERGES`** and **`<PREFIX>_ALTCLS_FACTORED`** — counts of
alternation runs merged into one class and prefix-factored
(`tuning.md` §2.6, §2.7). Emitted before either engine is built, so they are
on every artifact, a DFA-only one included.

```c
#define RX_ALTCLS_MERGES   1   /* alternation runs merged into one class */
#define RX_ALTCLS_FACTORED 0   /* alternation runs prefix-factored */
```

---

<a id="s7"></a>
## 7. The compile entry takes a NUL-terminated pattern

```c
int pcrec_compile(const char *pattern, const pcrec_options *opt,
                  pcrec_output *out, pcrec_error *err);
```

<a id="s7-p1"></a>[7¶1] `pcrec_compile()` takes a NUL-terminated pattern and no length. **A raw `0x00`
byte inside the intended pattern silently truncates the compile**: the 3-byte
pattern `"a\0b"` compiles as the 1-byte pattern `"a"` and `pcrec_compile()`
reports success. This is the documented behaviour of a NUL-terminated entry,
not a defect this API shape will fix.

- <a id="s7-p2"></a>[7¶2] **PCRE2's `PCRE2_ZERO_TERMINATED` mode truncates identically.** Measured
  against libpcre2 10.46 (through `tests/fuzz/pcre2_abi.h`): the buffer
  `{'a', 0, 'b'}` compiled with `PCRE2_ZERO_TERMINATED` matches only `"a"` (a
  1-byte match at the start of the subject `"a\0b"`), while with `length=3` it
  matches the whole subject, `[0,3)`. The difference is an API-surface gap —
  PCRE2 also accepts a true length and `pcrec_compile()` does not — not a
  difference in NUL semantics.
- <a id="s7-p3"></a>[7¶3] **`rx_info.pattern_len` records what was compiled**: the byte count
  `pcrec_compile()` saw, i.e. the truncated count. Compiling the byte-built
  3-byte `"a\0b"` through `pcrec_compile()` produces `out.c_src` containing
  `.pattern_len = 1,` (`tests/cli/run_cli_tests.sh` case16; the CLI cannot
  carry a NUL through `argv`). `pattern_len` is the SOURCE byte count, not a
  count of bytes the matcher walks (`'a\nb'`: `pattern_len = 4`; pinned in
  `tests/codegen/run_codegen_tests.sh`). Reading it needs the artifact
  compiled and linked, or a string search of `out.c_src`.
- <a id="s7-p4"></a>[7¶4] **The pre-flight a caller should run** when it knows the pattern's true
  length independently (as a caller with untrusted or NUL-bearing pattern
  text does):

  ```c
  if (strlen(pattern) != known_length) { /* the pattern contains a NUL:
                                            refuse it yourself */ }
  ```

  Nothing in `pcrec_compile()`'s signature enforces it.
- <a id="s7-p5"></a>[7¶5] **A length-taking compile** — a `(pattern, length)` entry that refuses a
  pattern whose declared extent it cannot verify — is not part of this
  contract; it is scheduled with `[DD-3]` and tracked as
  `docs/dev/known_issues.md` K9.

---

<a id="s8"></a>
## 8. The library entry: `pcrec_options`, `pcrec_output`, `pcrec_error`

<a id="s8-0"></a>
### 8.0 A complete compile

<a id="s8-0-p1"></a>[8.0¶1] This calling sequence compiles and runs as written (built
`gcc -Wall -Wextra -Werror` against `lib/pcrec.h` and `libpcrec.a`, run, and its
`matcher.c`/`matcher.h` output compiled in turn):

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include "pcrec.h"

int main(void)
{
    pcrec_options opt;
    pcrec_output  out;
    pcrec_error   err;

    /* MANDATORY first step: a zero-initialized pcrec_options has
       prefix == NULL and every compile fails with "invalid symbol prefix". */
    pcrec_default_options(&opt);
    opt.header_name = "matcher.h";   /* NULL (the default) = self-contained .c */

    if (pcrec_compile("a(b|c)+d", &opt, &out, &err) != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "pcrec: %s (at byte %zu of the %s)\n", err.msg, err.pos,
                err.input == PCREC_ERR_INPUT_PATTERN ? "pattern" : "template");
        return 1;
    }

    /* out.c_src and out.h_src are malloc'd, NUL-terminated C source and are
       the CALLER's to free from here on. h_src is non-NULL exactly when
       opt.header_name was set. */
    FILE *c = fopen("matcher.c", "w");
    if (c) { fputs(out.c_src, c); fclose(c); }
    if (out.h_src) {
        FILE *h = fopen("matcher.h", "w");
        if (h) { fputs(out.h_src, h); fclose(h); }
    }

    pcrec_output_free(&out);   /* frees both buffers, NULLs both fields */
    return 0;
}
```

<a id="s8-0-p2"></a>[8.0¶2] **Link with `-Wl,--gc-sections` (GNU ld) or `-Wl,-dead_strip` (ld64).**
`libpcrec.a` is a static archive in which `.rxt`-source support (the
composer) is statically reachable from the ordinary compile path, so a
consumer that never calls `pcrec_compile_defs` / `pcrec_rxt_source_parse`
pulls those objects in unless the linker drops unreachable sections. Measured:
the flag, with no source change, recovers 43,968 of the 44,448 bytes those
objects add to a minimal consumer's `__text`, leaving 480 bytes and two symbols
the composer's early-return path still reaches. Omitting it is not wrong, only
larger.

<a id="s8-0-p3"></a>[8.0¶3] Four things in the example are contract:

1. <a id="s8-0-p4"></a>[8.0¶4] **`pcrec_default_options()` is mandatory.** A zeroed `pcrec_options` has
   `prefix == NULL`, which pcrec refuses: a `memset`-zeroed struct returns `-1`
   with `err.msg == "invalid symbol prefix (must be a C identifier, <= 60
   chars)"` for a pattern that compiles after `pcrec_default_options()`. It
   sets `prefix = "rx"`, `encoding = PCREC_ENC_BYTE` (`0`) and
   `header_name = NULL`, and zeroes everything else (`flags = 0`,
   `engine = 0`); override fields after calling it, never instead.
2. <a id="s8-0-p5"></a>[8.0¶5] **`pcrec_output` owns two heap buffers and the caller frees them.**

   ```c
   typedef struct {
       char *c_src;   /* malloc'd; free with pcrec_output_free */
       char *h_src;   /* malloc'd, or NULL when options.header_name == NULL */
   } pcrec_output;
   ```

   `pcrec_output_free()` frees both and NULLs both fields, so it is safe to
   call twice and safe when `h_src` was never produced. There is no other way
   to release them. This is the compile path's lifecycle; the match path has
   none (§5.2).
3. <a id="s8-0-p6"></a>[8.0¶6] **`h_src` is non-NULL exactly when `header_name` was set.** Test `h_src`.
4. <a id="s8-0-p7"></a>[8.0¶7] **Check the return value, not the error struct.** `pcrec_compile()` returns
   `0` on success (`out` filled) and `-1` on failure, filling `err` (if
   non-NULL) only on failure.

<a id="s8-1"></a>
### 8.1 What `pcrec_compile()` guarantees its caller (D56)

- <a id="s8-1-p1"></a>[8.1¶1] **It never `abort()`s the caller on the compile path.** Every allocation
  site routes failure through the internal `pcrec_ctx_nomem()` and returns a
  normal `-1` with a diagnostic, so a caller that sets a memory limit to
  survive a hostile pattern survives it. A compile under memory pressure never
  returns success with a degraded artifact: an allocation failure on a
  non-final internal attempt (the size-term ladder, an `--engine=auto` DFA
  overflow retry, a size-cap retry rung) is reported as `-1`, never absorbed
  by a later attempt (K60, D109), and the emitted DFA state legend's scratch
  storage lives in the compile's arena, so a failure there is an ordinary
  refusal (K60, D105). Measured: `make alloc`'s witnesses W1, W3 and W4 absorb
  0 forced failures. The DFA structural invariants refuse through
  `pcrec_ctx_fail` like every other "cannot happen" site (K61). The one
  `abort()` left in the library is on the syntax-dump path's detached string
  buffers, which run outside a compile and have no `pcrec_error` to report
  through. The emitted bytes of a compile that does not run out of memory do
  not depend on any of this.
- <a id="s8-1-p2"></a>[8.1¶2] **A pattern can be refused for compile-side RESOURCE reasons**, a failure
  class distinct from a syntax error that arrives through the same `-1` and
  `pcrec_error`; a caller tells them apart by `err.msg`. Measured: `a{9795}`
  compiles; `a{9796}` returns `-1` with `err.msg == "pattern too complex for
  the DFA engine (subset construction exceeds 48000000 state-set elements; try
  --engine=vm)"`. The pattern is legal PCRE; compiling it would cost more than
  pcrec spends. A caller that reports every `-1` as bad syntax is wrong here.
  The escape the message names is real: the same `a{9796}` compiles under
  `--engine=vm`, which never builds that DFA. The compile budgets and their
  overrides are `limits.md`'s.

<a id="s8-2"></a>
### 8.2 The option and error structures

<a id="s8-2-p1"></a>[8.2¶1] `pcrec_options`, all twenty-five members in declaration order; the comment
beside each is a one-line gloss, and the full text is `lib/pcrec.h`'s own
comment and, for a tuning axis, `docs/spec/tuning.md` §2:

```c
typedef struct {
    const char *prefix;      /* C identifier prefix; default "rx" */
    int         encoding;    /* PCREC_ENC_* ; PER-COMPILE-CALL, see below */
    uint64_t    flags;       /* PCREC_CASELESS | PCREC_EMIT_MAIN |
                                 PCREC_NO_CAPTURES | PCREC_TRACE | the
                                 optimization-axis deny/force bits — the
                                 catalogue is tuning.md §2, see below */
    const char *header_name; /* NULL = self-contained .c */
    int         engine;      /* PCREC_ENGINE_AUTO / _DFA / _VM */
    int64_t     step_budget; /* PCREC_STEP_BUDGET_DEFAULT / _NONE, or a count */
    int64_t     work_budget; /* PCREC_WORK_BUDGET_DEFAULT / _NONE, or a count */
    int         unroll_k;    /* PCREC_UNROLL_K_DEFAULT (0) = built-in default */
    int         vm_entry_shape; /* PCREC_VM_ENTRY_AUTO (0) / _PLAIN / _SHARED
                                    / _FORWARD / _INLINE — an ORDINAL rung,
                                    not a bit; tuning.md §2.21 */
    int         frame_capacity; /* 0 = let the compiler size it. NOT the
                                    same sentinel as rx_info's field of the
                                    same name, which uses -1 for unbounded */
    uint64_t    max_emit_code_bytes; /* RAISE-ONLY cap override; 0 = built-in */
    uint64_t    max_emit_bytes;      /* RAISE-ONLY cap override; 0 = built-in */
    uint64_t    max_nfa_states;      /* RAISE-ONLY compile budget; 0 = built-in */
    uint64_t    max_dfa_states_goto; /* RAISE-ONLY compile budget; 0 = built-in */
    uint64_t    max_subset_elems;    /* RAISE-ONLY compile budget; 0 = built-in */
    uint64_t    max_auto_dfa_elems;  /* RAISE-ONLY; the AUTO route's DFA
                                        attempt budget only; 0 = built-in */
    uint64_t    warn_emit_bytes;     /* ADVISORY stderr warning, never a
                                        refusal; 0 DISABLES it. Lowerable,
                                        unlike the caps above */
    const char *name;        /* what rx_info.name reports; NULL = use prefix */
    int         tune;        /* PCREC_TUNE_MIN_SIZE .. _MAX_SPEED, -2..+2,
                                0 = balanced and a structural no-op */
        const char *features;    /* enabled feature-module set for THIS call;
                                 same vocabulary as --features; NULL = no
                                 request (see below) */
    const char        *analysis;            /* the findings ANALYSIS (bundle
                                               name); NULL = the built-in
                                               default alone */
    const char *const *analysis_dirs;       /* NULL-terminated directory
                                               list searched for NAME.rxt;
                                               NULL = none */
    const char        *analysis_source;     /* .rxt TEXT holding bundles,
                                               parsed with no file access */
    size_t             analysis_source_len; /* its length in bytes */
    const char        *memfn;               /* the search-code kit's opaque
                                               option string (--memfn=);
                                               NULL or "" = none */
} pcrec_options;
```

- <a id="s8-2-p2"></a>[8.2¶2] **The six `max_*` members are RAISE-ONLY**: a value below the built-in
  default is refused as a malformed option, so no caller can use one to
  manufacture a refusal. `warn_emit_bytes` is not raise-only: it never refuses,
  so lowering it cannot break a build. `docs/spec/limits.md` is their home.
- <a id="s8-2-p3"></a>[8.2¶3] **`encoding` is a PER-COMPILE-CALL scalar** (D58), carried in this field and
  nowhere else — no process-global, file-global or environment variable — so
  mixing encodings in one compilation unit or one binary is supported: each
  artifact carries its own prefix and exactly one encoding's residual block.
  Values and semantics: §9.1.
- <a id="s8-2-p4"></a>[8.2¶4] **`frame_capacity`'s `0`** means "let the compiler size it"
  ([sentinel](#s6-p15)).
- <a id="s8-2-p5"></a>[8.2¶5] **`name`** is what `rx_info.name` reports; `NULL` uses the prefix.
- <a id="s8-2-p6"></a>[8.2¶6] **`analysis`, `analysis_dirs`, `analysis_source`, `analysis_source_len`**
  choose the findings analysis a compile reads its byte rates from, resolved
  `analysis_source` first, then `DIR/<name>.rxt` for each of `analysis_dirs`,
  then the analyses built into the library, always ending in the built-in
  `default`. An analysis changes speed, never an answer or a give-up; a name
  that resolves nowhere, a malformed bundle or an include cycle refuses the
  compile through `pcrec_error`. The chosen bundle's NAME is stamped into the
  artifact (`<PREFIX>_FINDINGS`). `docs/spec/findings.md` is their contract.
- <a id="s8-2-p7"></a>[8.2¶7] **`memfn`** is one opaque comma-separated string (e.g. `"no-NAME"` denies a
  kit row), validated once per compile by the kit's own parser, whose refusal
  text pcrec shows unchanged. An option belonging to the SIMD layer is accepted
  and inert under `-fno-memfn-simd` (the default). It is not a flag bit and
  does not move `rx_info.flags`.

<a id="s8-2-p8"></a>[8.2¶8] **`features`** applies the CLI's `--features` lever per `pcrec_compile()` call:
a comma-separated module-name list spelled as `pcrec --list-syntax`'s `module`
column, the frozen named set `"std1"` (D37), `"all"`, or `"none"`. An unknown
name is refused by name, through `pcrec_error`, with the wording the CLI's
`--features: <text>` line quotes minus that prefix.

- <a id="s8-2-p9"></a>[8.2¶9] **`NULL` means "make no request"** and is NOT the CLI's bare-invocation
  default: a caller that never sets the field gets the ungated compile with no
  module enabled. A caller that wants the CLI's behaviour passes `"std1"` or
  the exported constant `pcrec_default_features`. The CLI always assigns a
  concrete value (`features ? features : pcrec_default_features`), so a bare
  `pcrec` invocation is unaffected.
- <a id="s8-2-p10"></a>[8.2¶10] **Applying it touches no shared state** (D19): concurrent `pcrec_compile()`
  calls with different `features` cannot race, because each resolves its
  request into its own compile's state. The CLI's own `--features`
  additionally installs a process-global its other query surfaces
  (`--probe-ask`, `--count-groups`, `--list-source`) read; this field affects
  only its own call.

<a id="s8-2-p11"></a>[8.2¶11] **Every boolean option is one representation end-to-end**
(`PCREC_CASELESS`, `PCREC_EMIT_MAIN`, `PCREC_NO_CAPTURES`, `PCREC_TRACE`,
`PCREC_UCP`, and the strategy deny/force bits): the bit a CLI flag sets,
carried in `pcrec_options.flags` and reflected in `rx_info.flags` unless
deliberately masked (§6, [flags](#s6-p16)).

- <a id="s8-2-p12"></a>[8.2¶12] `PCREC_NO_CAPTURES` gives the pure-DFA, `<PREFIX>_NCAPS 1` artifact;
  captures are on by default.
- <a id="s8-2-p13"></a>[8.2¶13] `PCREC_UCP` (bit 34) is `PCRE2_UCP`'s semantics (`docs/spec/cli.md`
  `--ucp`); it changes answers, so it is not masked. A pattern that turns UCP
  on inside itself with `(*UCP)` does not set the bit, as an inline `(?i)` does
  not set `PCREC_CASELESS`; `rx_info.pattern` records it.
- <a id="s8-2-p14"></a>[8.2¶14] `docs/spec/tuning.md` §2 is the axis-bit catalogue (bit, CLI spelling, what
  it denies or forces, whether it is masked) and §4 maps every bit to its
  `pcrec_options` field. `lib/pcrec.h`'s comments are the implementation's own
  record of the same facts, not their authority.

<a id="s8-2-p15"></a>[8.2¶15] **`pcrec_error`** carries which input a diagnostic's `pos` indexes into:

```c
typedef enum {
    PCREC_ERR_INPUT_PATTERN  = 0,
    PCREC_ERR_INPUT_TEMPLATE = 1
} pcrec_err_input;

typedef struct {
    char            msg[256];
    size_t          pos;
    pcrec_err_input input;
} pcrec_error;
```

<a id="s8-2-p16"></a>[8.2¶16] `pcrec_compile()` always sets `input = PCREC_ERR_INPUT_PATTERN`; a future
substitution-template compiler is the first producer of
`PCREC_ERR_INPUT_TEMPLATE`. Measured: the unterminated group `"a(b"` returns
`-1` with `err.pos == 1`, `err.input == PCREC_ERR_INPUT_PATTERN`.
`pcrec_compile()` is safe to call concurrently (§5.3, TS-3).

---

<a id="s9"></a>
## 9. Encodings, character positions and subject validity

<a id="s9-1"></a>
### 9.1 The two encodings

<a id="s9-1-p1"></a>[9.1¶1] `PCREC_ENC_BYTE` (`0`, the default; CLI `-e byte`) and `PCREC_ENC_UTF8` (`1`;
`-e utf8`) both compile; the value is what `rx_info.encoding` reports. Any
other value is refused with `"unknown encoding (want byte, utf8)"`, an
ordinary `-1`-with-diagnostic return that writes no C (`-e ascii` is an
unknown encoding). The CLI spells the option `-e NAME` or `--encoding=NAME`.

- <a id="s9-1-p2"></a>[9.1¶2] **`byte`**: every byte, `0x80` and up included, is one character with no
  case and no meaning attached. Every position is a character boundary and
  every byte string is well-formed, so the guards of §9.2 and §9.4 are not
  emitted.
- <a id="s9-1-p3"></a>[9.1¶3] **`utf8`**: a character is one to four bytes, and `.` and a class match a
  whole character. By default an ill-formed sequence in the SUBJECT matches
  nothing and is not reported (§9.3; the `PCRE2_MATCH_INVALID_UTF` semantics);
  `-futf-check` refuses it instead (§9.4). The full semantic contract is
  `docs/design/utf8_design.md` §2.6/§2.6.1.
- <a id="s9-1-p4"></a>[9.1¶4] **The encoding reaches the parser in one place**: a code point above `0xFF`
  written `\x{…}` is a compile error under `byte` and compiles under `utf8`
  (`docs/design/utf8_design.md` §2.7.3).
- <a id="s9-1-p5"></a>[9.1¶5] `<prefix>_next_pos` (§3.1.1) and `<prefix>_valid_upto` (§3.1.2) carry each
  encoding's caller-facing residue; a caller's code compiles unchanged across
  encodings.

<a id="s9-2"></a>
### 9.2 `startpos` must be a character boundary, and by default the artifact enforces it

<a id="s9-2-p1"></a>[9.2¶1] The axis is `tuning.md` §2.23; the stamp is `<PREFIX>_STARTPOS_GUARD`
(§6.3.6). Under an encoding with multi-byte characters, a `startpos > 0` inside
a character is REFUSED with `PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS`, below `PCREC_ERR_FLOOR` and
not a give-up: nothing is attempted and no budget is spent. The test is O(1)
and reads at most one byte of `s`.

- <a id="s9-2-p2"></a>[9.2¶2] **This is libpcre2's shape.** Under `PCRE2_UTF` every mid-character
