  `startoffset` returns `PCRE2_ERROR_BADUTFOFFSET`: measured over ten patterns
  at both mid-character offsets of a two-character subject, 20 of 20 refused,
  with the same patterns answering normally at all three boundary offsets
  (`docs/design/utf8_measurements/out/startbnd.txt` §2, libpcre2 10.46). Under
  D26 pcrec owes the refusal, not the number.
- <a id="s9-2-p3"></a>[9.2¶3] **A caller-passed `startpos` naming a continuation byte is refused whether
  that byte is inside a well-formed character or a stray** (libpcre2 draws no
  line either: `docs/dev/k75_measurement.md`).
- <a id="s9-2-p4"></a>[9.2¶4] **`startpos > n` still returns `0`**, and every position at or beyond `n`
  is a boundary. libpcre2 answers `PCRE2_ERROR_BADOFFSET` there; pcrec keeps
  its answer, a deliberate divergence.
- <a id="s9-2-p5"></a>[9.2¶5] **The anchored entries carry the same guard** against `ctx->pos`, and the
  `_in` entries inherit it from the bodies they share, so no entry reaches the
  permissive behaviour.
- <a id="s9-2-p6"></a>[9.2¶6] **`<prefix>_next_pos` is the supported way to produce a valid `startpos`**,
  and the find-all loop (§3.1) uses it on both arms, so the loop never meets
  the guard.
- <a id="s9-2-p7"></a>[9.2¶7] **`-fno-startpos-guard` selects the other semantics**: the artifact answers
  at whatever position the caller named, with the automaton's own answer. For
  a leading NEGATIVE assertion that answer differs from both of PCRE2's UTF
  modes in the succeeding direction — `(?<!.)` at offset 1 of the four bytes
  `CE B1 CE B2` reports `(1,1)` — because a truncated leading character has no
  path and a negative assertion succeeds where its body has none.
- <a id="s9-2-p8"></a>[9.2¶8] **Neither arm ROUNDS a caller's `startpos > 0`.** A caller handed an answer
  for a position it did not ask about could not tell it from an answer for the
  one it did.

<a id="s9-2-p9"></a>[9.2¶9] **`-fstartpos-guard=align` is the rounding, asked for by name** (D133,
`tuning.md` §2.23). It is for a caller holding a misaligned pointer into valid
text, one that split a buffer on arbitrary bytes. A `startpos > 0` inside a
character is moved FORWARD over continuation bytes to the next character
start (or `n`), once, at entry, and the search runs exactly as if that
position had been passed: `caps` offsets, `\G` and a lookbehind's context are
read from it. Offset 0 is never moved. The anchored entries answer `-1` at a
misaligned `ctx->pos`, because no match begins inside a character. It cannot be
combined with `-fno-startpos-guard`, and it is inert under `byte`. It does not
accept invalid UTF-8: under `-futf-check` the check runs from the ALIGNED
position, stepping back behind it as for any `startpos`, so the bytes of the
character the pointer landed inside are checked as the caller's text.

<a id="s9-3"></a>
### 9.3 Offset 0 on an ill-formed subject

<a id="s9-3-p1"></a>[9.3¶1] **Offset 0 is never refused, and on a subject that begins with continuation
bytes it is not where a match is attempted** (K73). No character precedes
offset 0, but a subject may BEGIN with continuation bytes (`0x80`-`0xBF`), and
then offset 0 is not a character start. The search then begins at the first
non-continuation byte (or at `n`), as `PCRE2_MATCH_INVALID_UTF` advances its
start offset, and every answer is the answer from there: `''`, `\B`, `x*` and
`(?=)` report `(1,1)` on `\x80` and `(2,2)` on `\x80\x80`; `^`, `\A` and `\G`
are FALSE at the moved start, so `^` finds nothing on `\x80` and `\G|b` reports
`(2,3)` on `\x80\x80b` (libpcre2 10.46,
`docs/dev/lanes/k73utf_evidence/k73_witness_10.46.txt`). An ill-formed LEAD
byte (`0xFF`, a truncated `0xE3`) is a valid start and is attempted.

- <a id="s9-3-p2"></a>[9.3¶2] The rule has no flag: it is the same under `-fno-startpos-guard`, which
  governs only a `startpos > 0`. An explicit mid-character `startpos > 0` keeps
  §9.2's refusal, a deliberate divergence from `PCRE2_MATCH_INVALID_UTF`.
- <a id="s9-3-p3"></a>[9.3¶3] **The anchored entries answer `-1` at `ctx->pos == 0` on such a subject**,
  because they report only a match beginning exactly at `ctx->pos`. libpcre2
  under `PCRE2_ANCHORED` advances there and reports the match at the moved
  start (`(1,1)` for `x*` on `\x80`); pcrec's anchored contract cannot report a
  start other than `ctx->pos`, a second stated divergence on which both entry
  shapes agree.

<a id="s9-4"></a>
### 9.4 `-futf-check`: refusing an ill-formed subject

<a id="s9-4-p1"></a>[9.4¶1] By default an artifact is INVALID-TOLERANT (§9.3). An artifact compiled with
`-futf-check` (`tuning.md` §2.36, `docs/design/utf_valid_design.md`, D133;
stamp `<PREFIX>_UTF_CHECK`) refuses a call with `PCREC_ERR_UTF` when an
ill-formed sequence BEGINS anywhere in `[f, n)`, where `f` is `startpos`
stepped back LB characters — before any attempt, and whether or not a match
lies before the bad bytes (`a` on `a\xff` is refused, as libpcre2 10.46 refuses
it). Otherwise the call answers exactly as the default artifact does.

- <a id="s9-4-p2"></a>[9.4¶2] **LB is PCRE2's `max_lookbehind` fact** (measured on 10.46): the widest
  lookbehind branch in characters, and 1 for `\b`, `\B` and `\A`; never summed
  through nesting; dead code (a `(?(DEFINE)…)` body) counts. `^`, `$`, `\G`,
  `\z`, `\Z` and `\K` count 0. So `b` on `\xffab` from 2 answers `(2,3)` while
  `(?<=..)b` there is refused.
- <a id="s9-4-p3"></a>[9.4¶3] **The step-back is PCRE2's raw walk**: per character, one byte back and then
  back over every continuation byte, clamped at 0 and not validated.
- <a id="s9-4-p4"></a>[9.4¶4] **Order: the boundary guard first, then the check** (measured on 10.46). A
  mid-character `startpos > 0` is `PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS` whether or not the
  subject is well-formed; under `-fstartpos-guard=align` the check runs from
  the aligned position. `startpos > n` keeps `0` and is not checked. At
  `startpos == 0` the guard does not refuse, so a subject that BEGINS with a
  continuation byte is refused by the check at offset 0.
- <a id="s9-4-p5"></a>[9.4¶5] **Every entry that takes a subject checks, at one site per body**, beside
  the boundary guard, so the anchored entries and the `_in` entries return
  `PCREC_ERR_UTF` on exactly the calls `<prefix>_search` refuses from the same
  position. A FRAMES escalation of the tiered default entry re-runs the body and
  validates a second time.
- <a id="s9-4-p6"></a>[9.4¶6] **The cost is one O(n) pass per call** (`docs/design/utf_valid_design.md`
  §5: about as much again as a scanning call on sparse-accented text, and it
  makes a call a prefilter answers sublinearly linear), which is why it is off
  by default. A find-all loop over a checking artifact validates on every call;
  §3.1.2 gives the linear idiom.
- <a id="s9-4-p7"></a>[9.4¶7] **Inert under `byte`**: no check is emitted, `<PREFIX>_UTF_CHECK` reads
  `"inert"`, and the artifact is byte-identical to one built without the flag.

<a id="s9-4-p8"></a>[9.4¶8] **A stated divergence: `PCRE2_UTF` clips backward reads at `f`; pcrec does
not** (D142; measured on libpcre2 10.46 and 10.48). Under `PCRE2_UTF`, libpcre2
treats `f` as the START OF THE SUBJECT for a lookbehind's or `\b`'s backward
reads, even on well-formed text: `(?<=\ba)b` on `"xab"` from `startpos` 2
reports `(2,3)` under `PCRE2_UTF` though it finds nothing from 0 and nothing
without UTF; `(?<=(?<=..)a)b` on `"zzzab"` from 4 finds nothing under
`PCRE2_UTF` and reports `(4,5)` without it. pcrec reads the real bytes, with or
without `-futf-check`, and answers as the default artifact does (no match and
`(4,5)` above): a match's answer must not depend on where the caller started
the search. The refusal set and the refusal OFFSET are exact and unaffected;
only the accepted ANSWER differs, and only for patterns whose backward reach
exceeds LB (three patterns in the pinned set). The class is 4 cells per configuration, pinned EXACTLY (`CLIP` in
`tests/utfcheck/check.py`, the `clip-*` populations; reproducers in
`docs/dev/lanes/uvbuild_report.md` §3.1/§5, the class described in
`tests/utfcheck/CLAUDE.md`), so a change in either engine moves a number
rather than a sentence (D26: a deliberate, stated divergence is the only
allowed exception to exact matching semantics).

<a id="s9-5"></a>
### 9.5 Positions the engine generates

<a id="s9-5-p1"></a>[9.5¶1] **Every position the ENGINE generates is a character start of the encoding**,
unconditionally and under every setting of the guard: an unanchored search's
candidate match starts, a failed attempt's retry, and a search's first attempt
at offset 0 (§9.3). A reported match span never begins inside a character, on
any subject. The guard axis governs only where a CALLER may point an entry.

---

<a id="s10"></a>
## 10. Working storage: the `_in` entries and the tiered default

<a id="s10-p1"></a>[10¶1] A generated matcher never allocates (§5.2). The two arrays a backtracking
match needs — the RESUME STACK and its undo TRAIL — are sized at compile time,
which makes an artifact's depth ceiling a compile-time constant. A caller may
supply the storage instead, keeping the never-allocates property while lifting
the ceiling as far as it is willing to reserve (D71 item 2;
`docs/design/frame_buffer_design.md` has the alternatives and measurements).
Checked by `tests/recursion/framebuffer.rxt` (behaviour), `tests/codegen/
run_codegen_tests.sh`'s `[DD-14.FB]` block (the six entry declarations
byte-exact, the sizing surface on both engines, no capacity guard reading a
stamped constant, the delegation direction), `tests/thread/
run_stackdepth_tests.sh` (the 128 KB thread), all in `make test`, and
`make test-frame-buffer` on demand (the NULL-equivalence spread and §10.6's
reservation).

<a id="s10-1"></a>
### 10.1 The default ceiling

- <a id="s10-1-p1"></a>[10.1¶1] **The depth ceiling is small, and it is a SUBJECT SIZE.** Measured on a
  default `-p rx --features all` build of `^(a(?1)?b)$` (recursion depth grows
  with the subject): it matches up to a 684-byte subject and returns
  `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` at a 686-byte one. libpcre2 10.46 matches 800 KB of the
  same shape (cited from `docs/design/subroutines_design.md` §5.6).
- <a id="s10-1-p2"></a>[10.1¶2] **The refusal is constant-time.** Measured on the same build, the
  left-recursive runaway `^(a|(?1)a)$` over aⁿb returns `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` in
  0.0006 s at every n from 100 to 100,000. libpcre2 pays a cost growing as the
  square of the subject there (2.6–5.6 s at n = 20,000; the same section
  measures the exponent at 2.04). A caller who wants the depth buys it with
  §10.6.

<a id="s10-2"></a>
### 10.2 The three entries and the descriptor

```c
typedef struct {
    void   *frames;    /* storage for resume frames */
    size_t  nframes;   /* CAPACITY IN FRAMES — not bytes */
    void   *trail;     /* storage for trail entries */
    size_t  ntrail;    /* capacity in ENTRIES — not bytes */
} <prefix>_buffers;

int       <prefix>_search_in    (const unsigned char *s, size_t n, size_t startpos,
                                 ptrdiff_t (*caps)[2], const <prefix>_buffers *buf);
ptrdiff_t <prefix>_match_in     (const rx_ctx *ctx, const <prefix>_buffers *buf);
ptrdiff_t <prefix>_match_caps_in(const rx_ctx *ctx, ptrdiff_t (*caps_out)[2],
                                 const <prefix>_buffers *buf);
```

<a id="s10-2-p1"></a>[10.2¶1] Each `_in` entry is its un-suffixed sibling in every respect — anchoring,
return space, `caps`/`caps_out` discipline, give-up codes, the boundary guard
and the UTF check (§3, §4, §5, §9 apply unchanged) — plus one argument naming
where the working storage lives. Every artifact exports all three.

- <a id="s10-2-p2"></a>[10.2¶2] **`<prefix>_buffers` is PER-ARTIFACT, scoped by the prefix** — not a
  fixed-literal `rx_*` type, because a resume frame's SIZE differs between
  artifacts (measured: 24 bytes without a LINKED call, 40 with one,
  `RX_VM_CALL_LINKED > 0`; a SPLICED call, `RX_VM_CALL_SPLICED`, is inlined and
  adds nothing, so the email specimen's factored form under `--engine=vm`
  stamps 24 with ten spliced calls). Read the stamp; never infer it from the
  pattern text.
- <a id="s10-2-p3"></a>[10.2¶3] **The counts are CAPACITIES, not byte sizes**: `nframes` frames, `ntrail`
  trail entries. §10.4 converts bytes to counts.
- <a id="s10-2-p4"></a>[10.2¶4] **`frames` and `trail` are two separate regions and both are required** when
  `buf` is non-NULL. The trail is not a detail of the frames: measured on
  `^(a(?1)?b)$` the trail binds first at the stamped defaults, so raising only
  `nframes` would change nothing (`docs/design/frame_buffer_design.md` §4).

<a id="s10-3"></a>
### 10.3 `buf == NULL`, and what a give-up means

- <a id="s10-3-p1"></a>[10.3¶1] **`buf == NULL` is exactly a call to the un-suffixed entry** with the same
  other arguments — the same call, which an artifact may implement as one. It
  therefore gets the tiered default of §10.9.
- <a id="s10-3-p2"></a>[10.3¶2] **A give-up means "the buffer in use ran out", and does not say whose.**
  `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` is returned for a caller buffer exactly as for the
  stamped default (§4). The count that would have sufficed is NOT reported: it
  is a diagnostic fact the default artifact carries no machinery to produce
  (D71 item 1).
- <a id="s10-3-p3"></a>[10.3¶3] **A give-up is RETRYABLE.** Calling the same entry again with the same
  subject and `startpos` and a larger buffer is defined: the matcher holds no
  state between calls (§5.3), `caps` is untouched on every negative return, and
  the buffers are scratch. "Give up, double the buffer, retry" is correct.
- <a id="s10-3-p4"></a>[10.3¶4] **The buffer's contents after any call are UNSPECIFIED.** A caller must not
  read them and need not re-initialise them.
- <a id="s10-3-p5"></a>[10.3¶5] **Alignment.** Both regions must be aligned for the artifact's frame and
  trail types; `<PREFIX>_BUFFER_ALIGN` states the requirement. Storage from
  `malloc`, `mmap`, or a declaration of any ordinary object type satisfies it
  on every target pcrec supports; the macro is for pointer arithmetic inside a
  larger arena.

<a id="s10-4"></a>
### 10.4 Sizing a buffer

<a id="s10-4-p1"></a>[10.4¶1] The frame and trail layouts are private to the artifact; what is published is
the arithmetic. Five macros, in the emitted HEADER, on every artifact:

```c
#define <PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAMES      2048  /* the stamped DEFAULT capacity */
#define <PREFIX>_TRAIL_FRAMES       3072
#define <PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAME_SIZE    40  /* bytes per frame, THIS artifact */
#define <PREFIX>_TRAIL_FRAME_SIZE     16
#define <PREFIX>_BUFFER_ALIGN          8
```

and four of the same facts as `rx_info` fields — `resume_frames`,
`trail_frames`, `resume_frame_size`, `trail_frame_size` (§6) — for a consumer
with no C header (an FFI or `dlopen` binding).

- <a id="s10-4-p2"></a>[10.4¶2] **The values are STAMPED FOR THE TARGET, not constants of pcrec.** A frame's
  size depends on the artifact — measured: 24 bytes call-free, 40 call-bearing,
  32 and 48 for the `--trace` versions of the same two — and on the target's
  type sizes. The numbers above are `^(a(?1)?b)$`'s. pcrec computes each from
  the same member list that emits the struct, and **the artifact ASSERTS each
  stamped macro against the real `sizeof`/`_Alignof` at its own build**, so a
  number computed for a different target model is a compile error naming the
  macro, not a silent under-allocation. Read the macros; never hardcode values.
- <a id="s10-4-p3"></a>[10.4¶3] **`<PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAMES` / `_TRAIL_FRAMES` are the stamped default
  capacities**: 2048/3072 on an artifact whose frame requirement is not
  statically bounded (D73), smaller where the compiler can bound it.
- <a id="s10-4-p4"></a>[10.4¶4] **A stamped size of `0` means "this engine takes no buffers" — test before
  dividing.** `bytes / <PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAME_SIZE` divides by zero on every DFA
  artifact. Pass `NULL` when the size is `0`; nothing is lost.
- <a id="s10-4-p5"></a>[10.4¶5] **On a DFA artifact the whole surface is present and inert**: the three
  `_in` entries, the `<prefix>_buffers` type and the five macros are emitted;
  the four sizing macros and the four `rx_info` fields read `0` (and
  `<PREFIX>_BUFFER_ALIGN` reads `1`); and an `_in`
  entry accepts a descriptor and ignores it, answering as its un-suffixed
  sibling. One call site therefore works against both engines. These five
  macros are on both engines, unlike the VM-only capacity macros of §6.3,
  because they are what a caller needs in order to CALL an entry.
- <a id="s10-4-p6"></a>[10.4¶6] `rx_info.resume_frames` carries the same number as `frame_capacity` for the
  bounded case; `frame_capacity` reports `-1` for "no bound at all"
  ([sentinel](#s6-p15)).

<a id="s10-5"></a>
### 10.5 Concurrency

<a id="s10-5-p1"></a>[10.5¶1] Each concurrent call, and each re-entrant call from a callout, needs its own
`<prefix>_buffers` regions, as it needs its own `caps`: §5.3.

<a id="s10-6"></a>
### 10.6 Example: an mmap'd, lazily-committed reservation

<a id="s10-6-p1"></a>[10.6¶1] The caller reserves address space it does not commit, and the operating system
materialises only the pages the match touches:

```c
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include "matcher.h"                  /* the generated header */

size_t bytes = (size_t)64 << 20;      /* 64 MB of address space, per region */
void  *f = mmap(NULL, bytes, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE,
                MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS|MAP_NORESERVE, -1, 0);
void  *t = mmap(NULL, bytes, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE,
                MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS|MAP_NORESERVE, -1, 0);

rx_buffers buf = { f, bytes / RX_RESUME_FRAME_SIZE,
                   t, bytes / RX_TRAIL_FRAME_SIZE };

int r = rx_search_in(subject, n, 0, caps, &buf);   /* pcrec allocates nothing */
```

<a id="s10-6-p2"></a>[10.6¶2] Measured on `^(a(?1)?b)$` with those two reservations
(`RX_RESUME_FRAME_SIZE == 40`, `RX_TRAIL_FRAME_SIZE == 16`, so 1,677,721 frames
and 4,194,304 trail entries; 1.8 MB resident before the first match):

| subject | result | time | process RSS after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 684 B | match | 0.0001 s | 2.0 MB |
| 200 KB | match | 0.0135 s | 24 MB |
| **800 KB** | **match** | **0.057 s** | **90 MB** |
| 932 KB | match | 0.065 s | 102 MB |
| 940 KB | `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` | 0.069 s | 103 MB |

<a id="s10-6-p3"></a>[10.6¶3] Through the un-suffixed `rx_search`, the same artifact matches the 684 B
subject and returns `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` on the four larger ones.
`tests/recursion/run_frame_buffer.sh` asserts these. 128 MB reserved costs
about 1.7 MB resident until touched; the 800 KB row is the depth libpcre2 10.46
reaches from its heap; and **the ceiling is predictable from the emitted
numbers**: the trail binds, at `ntrail / (trail entries per level)`, which for
this pattern is 4,194,304 / 8.98 ≈ 467,000 levels, and the measured boundary
lies between n = 466,000 and n = 470,000. The buffer need not be `mmap`'d: a
heap allocation, a static array in the caller's translation unit, or an arena
slice works.

<a id="s10-7"></a>
### 10.7 The freestanding and embedded profile

<a id="s10-7-p1"></a>[10.7¶1] A caller with no `mmap` and no heap has two routes:

- <a id="s10-7-p2"></a>[10.7¶2] **Pass `NULL`** and get the stamped default, on the stack.
- <a id="s10-7-p3"></a>[10.7¶3] **Point the descriptor at the caller's own static storage.** That does not
  violate §5.3's no-mutable-state rule, which binds what pcrec EMITS: storage
  the embedder declares is the embedder's, and the embedder knows whether its
  calls are concurrent. A single-context embedded caller puts the buffer in
  `.bss`, keeps its stack small, and pays nothing.

<a id="s10-8"></a>
### 10.8 What the `_in` entries do not change

- <a id="s10-8-p1"></a>[10.8¶1] `<prefix>_search`, `<prefix>_match` and `<prefix>_match_caps` keep their
  exact signatures, return spaces, anchoring and `caps` disciplines; a consumer
  that never calls an `_in` entry needs no source change, and its call sites
  are binary-compatible.
- <a id="s10-8-p2"></a>[10.8¶2] `<prefix>_next_pos` and the find-all protocol are untouched.
- <a id="s10-8-p3"></a>[10.8¶3] The code space of §4 gains no member: `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` covers the
  caller-buffer case.
- <a id="s10-8-p4"></a>[10.8¶4] No allocation is added anywhere (§5.2 stands, scoped to the match path).

<a id="s10-9"></a>
### 10.9 The tiered default of the un-suffixed entries

<a id="s10-9-p1"></a>[10.9¶1] **The rule.** On an artifact whose stamped default storage does not fit in one
4 KB page, each un-suffixed entry runs the match on a page-sized buffer of
`<PREFIX>_FAST_FRAMES` / `<PREFIX>_FAST_TRAIL` (§6.3.8) and, **on
`PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` and on no other outcome**, re-runs the same match from
scratch on the full stamped default, by calling a non-inlined internal
function that owns that storage. The second run's result is what the caller
gets. Every other outcome — a match, a no-match, `PCREC_ERR_STEPS`, `_WORK`,
`_RECURSE`, a below-the-floor code — is returned from the first run.
`-fno-tiered-entry` (`tuning.md` §2.12) restores the single-tier shape without
changing call sites.

<a id="s10-9-p2"></a>[10.9¶2] **An escalation restarts the step and work budgets.** They are per CALL, not
per tier: the second run begins with both full, as at the top of any call.
Carrying the remainder forward would be observably wrong — a deep run started
with a depleted budget would report `PCREC_ERR_STEPS` where a single-tier
artifact matches. Hence §4's rule that one call may spend up to twice each
budget, and the wasted fast attempt is bounded by those budgets rather than by
the fast frame count, since sixty frames of depth can absorb unbounded
backtracking.

<a id="s10-9-p3"></a>[10.9¶3] **No answer changes.** The deep run is a bit-for-bit replay of a single-tier
entry from scratch: the same capacities, both budgets refilled, the same
start-position loop over the same prefilter, one deterministic engine. Nothing
the fast attempt did can carry into it, because §5.3 leaves nothing that could
— the run state is a local of the tier that declared it, with no allocation,
no thread-local and no mutable static. For every artifact, subject and entry,
the value returned and the spans written are those of a single-tier entry. The
fast attempt may reach `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` where a single-tier run would have
reached `PCREC_ERR_STEPS`; that value is never returned (it is the escalation
trigger) and the replay reports `PCREC_ERR_STEPS`.

<a id="s10-9-p4"></a>[10.9¶4] **What a caller may rely on:**

- <a id="s10-9-p5"></a>[10.9¶5] Every promise of §3, §4 and §5 stands unchanged.
- <a id="s10-9-p6"></a>[10.9¶6] `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` from an un-suffixed entry means the STAMPED DEFAULT ran
  out, never the fast tier.
- <a id="s10-9-p7"></a>[10.9¶7] The depth an artifact can reach is unchanged (D73 keeps the stamped
  2048/3072); only the cost of not reaching it moved.
- <a id="s10-9-p8"></a>[10.9¶8] The `_in` entries have no tier: the caller owns the storage, so there is
  nothing to escalate from. `buf == NULL` is still the un-suffixed call and gets
  the tier.

<a id="s10-9-p9"></a>[10.9¶9] **What a caller must not rely on:** which tier answered. There is no
observable for it; `<PREFIX>_FAST_FRAMES` says where the boundary is, not
which side a call landed on.

<a id="s10-9-p10"></a>[10.9¶10] **The cost model.** Measured on the RFC 5322 email specimen (`--engine=vm`,
16-byte matching subject, N=100k, median of 5, `taskset`, six repetitions):
213–268 → 45.6–48.8 ns/call, against 44.2–47.2 for `<prefix>_search_in`, and
the entry's own frame (`gcc -fstack-usage`) 98,512 → 3,168 B. (The
`^(a(?1)?b)$` specimen of §5.3 and `limits.md` §5 is a different artifact with
different numbers: 131,216 → 3,184 B.) The tier is a bet that real calls hold
on the fast tier, and it loses on some patterns:

- <a id="s10-9-p11"></a>[10.9¶11] **The wasted fast attempt is bounded by the STEP and WORK budgets**, not by
  the frame count.
- <a id="s10-9-p12"></a>[10.9¶12] **There is a DISCONTINUITY at the boundary, not a ramp.** Measured on
  `((a)|(aa))+b` (tiered vs `-fno-tiered-entry`, N=20k, median of 5): 18.5 vs
  207.1 ns at n=1 (11× faster), 186.4 vs 365.3 at n=23, then 568.9 vs 372.9 at
  n=24 — a 3.05× jump across one byte, 1.53× slower than single-tier — and
  1.24–1.53× slower above it.
- <a id="s10-9-p13"></a>[10.9¶13] **"Deep" can mean a very short subject**: that boundary is a 25-byte subject
  (24 `a`s and a `b`). Depth is a property of the backtracking, not of the
  input length.
- <a id="s10-9-p14"></a>[10.9¶14] **An escalating call can do up to twice the step budget of work** (§4).

<a id="s10-9-p15"></a>[10.9¶15] A caller that knows its subjects are deep, or whose stack is too small for the
deep tier (§5.3, K33), supplies its own storage through the `_in` entries and
never meets the tier; `-fno-tiered-entry` is the answer for a workload measured
to sit above the boundary.
